articles.title: Hãng Trung Quốc ra mắt điện thoại "màn hình rộng" như Huawei Pura X View: Giá chưa tới 4 triệu nhưng nhìn ảnh thực tế mà hoảng luôn!
articles.text:
Cool X Wide mở bán ngày 8/11 tại Trung Quốc, là mẫu điện thoại màn hình rộng hiếm hoi trên thị trường hiện tại nhưng chất lượng có vẻ không ổn lắm.
Hãng điện thoại Coolpad của Trung Quốc vừa mở bán Cool X Wide, mẫu điện thoại Android đầu tiên theo dạng "khoát trực bản", tức thân máy rộng hơn hẳn điện thoại thông thường. Máy bán trên JD.com từ 10h ngày 8/11 với ba phiên bản: 8GB RAM và 128GB bộ nhớ giá 999 tệ (khoảng 3,8 triệu đồng), 8GB và 256GB giá 1.199 tệ (khoảng 4,6 triệu đồng), 12GB và 256GB giá 1.399 tệ (khoảng 5,4 triệu đồng).
Điểm khác biệt nằm ở màn hình. Cool X Wide dùng tấm LCD 6,38 inch tỷ lệ 16:10, thay cho tỷ lệ 20:9 dài và hẹp trên hầu hết điện thoại hiện nay. Thân máy rộng 94,5 mm, cao 150,3 mm, nặng 209 g. Màn hình rộng giúp xem phim ngang ít bị viền đen, đọc web hoặc truyện cũng hiển thị được nhiều chữ trên mỗi dòng hơn. Mặt lưng có cụm camera hình đường đua nằm ngang, kiểu dáng gần giống Huawei Pura X View, mẫu đã mở ra dòng điện thoại này.
Giá rẻ đồng nghĩa với việc nhiều thứ bị cắt giảm. Màn hình chỉ có độ phân giải 720 x 1158, tần số quét 90Hz, viền dưới khá dày. Chip MediaTek Helio G99 ra mắt từ tháng 5/2022, chỉ hỗ trợ mạng 4G, không có 5G. Máy có một camera sau 50 MP, pin 4600mAh, sạc nhanh 18W. Máy vẫn có hai SIM, khe thẻ nhớ microSD mở rộng tối đa 256GB và cảm biến vân tay đặt ở phím nguồn cạnh bên.
Một tính năng được Coolpad nhấn mạnh là chạy cùng lúc 8 tài khoản WeChat ngay trên hệ thống, không cần cài thêm ứng dụng nhân bản. Máy cũng hỗ trợ chia đôi màn hình. Với người bán hàng online hay quản lý nhiều tài khoản, đây là điểm dễ thấy nhất của chiếc máy này.
Cool X Wide chưa phải máy dành cho người cần hiệu năng. Các trang tin công nghệ Trung Quốc nhận xét máy hợp làm máy phụ để xem video, đọc sách hoặc quản lý nhiều tài khoản hơn là máy chính. Bề ngang 94,5 mm cũng khiến việc cầm một tay không còn thoải mái như các máy phổ biến.
Ngày bán ban đầu là 8/11, sau đó Coolpad xin lỗi vì giao hàng chậm. Hãng cho biết nguyên nhân nằm ở khâu sản xuất và xuất hàng, hàng sẽ được giao dần từ 15/11. Chưa có thông tin về việc máy được bán ngoài thị trường Trung Quốc.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security.
United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing
Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.
“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy
U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”
Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.
Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action
Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.
The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations
Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.
Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.
Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.
These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”
“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.title: Oura is acquiring medical AI chatbot startup Counsel Health
articles.text:
Oura announced its quarterly earnings today and said it agreed to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, after adding the company’s AI chatbot to its app earlier this year. Counsel Health calls itself an “AI-native primary care company,” using the app to deliver AI-generated responses and insights based on users’ health data reported from their wearables that can then proceed to a conversation with one of its in-house physicians.
Oura is acquiring medical AI chatbot startup Counsel Health
Doctor visits could start with a readout of your Oura ring data.
Oura says it expects the deal to close before the end of the year.
Oura CEO Tom Hale said in an interview with Bloomberg that the acquisition is part of a plan to connect wearables, clinical AI, and access to doctors based on insights from biometric data to answer questions or monitor ongoing conditions. Counsel Health’s AI chatbot can connect Oura users to a real doctor directly from the app and draw on users’ biometric data from their wearables in its answers to medical questions. The plan they describe in the press release is to focus on three areas, including preventative care, acute care for episodic health concerns, and specialty and chronic care for things like reproductive and cardiometabolic health.
According to Bloomberg, Counsel Health’s CEO Muthu Alagappan says it’s also planning to expand its network of on-demand physicians, which is currently “made up of about 50 people.” Counsel’s 70 employees will join Oura as part of the deal, with Alagappan becoming Oura’s chief clinical AI officer. Oura says in its announcement that Counsel will also continue offering its medical AI platform outside of Oura’s user base through new and existing enterprise partners, including “health plans, health systems, consumer health organizations, and employers.”

articles.title: Don't throw away your old phone box — you might need it in an emergency - Engadget
articles.text:
Don't throw away your old phone box — you might need it in an emergency
That cardboard box in your closet can come in handy more often than you’d think.
There's a specific type of anxiety that comes with deciding what to do with a box. Do you immediately throw it away? Do you stash it in a closet with about 20 other boxes that store little more than your own guilt? If you chuck it, you might need it for some unknown purpose in the future. But if you don't, that box might just sit in your home indefinitely.
It doesn't help when it's a nice box, either, like the type your phone might have arrived in. It's likely made of thick cardboard, with convenient compartments. Luckily, or perhaps unluckily for those who have finally gathered the nerve to go on a recycling tear, there are a few ways to help you decide the fate of your phone's box. Whether you're ready to resell your phone or need to report a stolen one, here's why you might want to keep your phone's box.
In case your phone gets stolen
Hopefully, you and your phone will never part ways without your consent. However, if it does get stolen, you'll need its IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) number. An IMEI is a 15- 17-digit number unique to your phone. Carriers can use it to identify the device and block it if it's lost or stolen. AT&T describes it as your phone's "fingerprint."
One place to check for your IMEI number is the box your phone came in. You should also be able to find it through your Apple or Google account, depending on the device you have. Still, in the heat of the moment, grabbing that box from a drawer might be the easiest option.
In case you need to return or resell your phone
Some less stressful scenarios might also lead you to keep your phone box. If you purchased an iPhone from Apple directly, for example, you have 14 days to return it from the day you received it. It must also be in the original packaging. Likewise, Samsung requires original packaging. Other retailers might have different policies, so at the very least, it's a good idea to check before you trash the box. Or keep it until after the window has closed, just to be safe.
Additionally, if you're thinking of reselling your phone at some point down the line, having its original box could come in handy. For one, you might have saved additional cables or something like a SIM ejector tool that a new owner will want. And while there's no hard data, some experts believe that having that original box can boost your odds of selling your phone at a good price.
Consumer Reports suggests the box increases the market value of the item and shows that you've taken good care of it. If you saw two identical iPhones for the same price, but only one was in a box, would you really choose the one without the box? The article also notes that you'll already have a box if you need to ship your phone.
So, if you're waffling on the eternal question of whether to save your phone's box, you can consider if any of those situations apply to you. And if not, there's likely a recycling bin somewhere waiting for its next deposit.

articles.title: Nvidia board hires ex-prosecutor Joon Kim to investigate Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Nvidia’s independent directors have hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate chief executive Jensen Huang. The board retained Joon H. Kim, a former acting US Attorney in Manhattan, and his firm to run it. The board announced the choice on Tuesday, CNBC reported.
“The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday,” the board said in a statement.
The board opened its own inquiry after Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at the chip buyer Megaspeed. US intelligence agencies have concluded she was a spy for China, which has rejected the claims. Huang would not take part in choosing counsel and would keep leading the company, a spokesman had said, according to the Times.
The Nvidia board has a combined 161 years of service, Kalley Huang and Don Clark reported for The New York Times. Huang, Tench Coxe and Harvey Jones have sat on it since 1993, according to Nvidia’s proxy statement.
Directors from the start
Sequoia Capital and Sutter Hill Ventures led a $2m round in Nvidia in 1993. Their investors, Mark Stevens and Coxe, then joined the board. Stevens left in 2006 and returned in 2008, the proxy shows. Brooke Seawell, a former Synopsys finance chief, joined in 1997. Jones and Seawell held Nvidia shares worth a combined $1.86bn as of June, the Times reported.
Before the hire, people familiar with the inquiry told the Financial Times it would probably be led by Stephen Neal, the lead independent director. Neal ran the law firm Cooley from 2001 to 2008 and is still its senior counsel. Cooley set up Nvidia in 1993 and has been its main outside counsel since, CNBC reported, citing the firm. Neal did not respond to CNBC.
Average director tenure is almost 15 years, nearly twice the S&P 500 norm, Semafor reported. No director is a current or former S&P 500 chief executive, and none has national security experience. None of the directors responded to the Times.
The rules on paper
Nvidia has a lead independent director instead of a board chair. The proxy says this gives each member “an equal voice”. Huang told Bloomberg’s Emily Chang that he skipped the chairman role so the chief executive could be held accountable, Bloomberg reported.
“Unlike many CEOs, I’m completely fireable,” Huang said.
Nvidia’s code of conduct tells staff and directors to avoid any activity that conflicts with the company’s interests, the proxy says. That includes anything that looks like a conflict. The company does not have a chief compliance officer, the filing confirms. Nvidia has said a committee of its finance, operations and human resources heads checks that staff follow its policies, Fortune reported.
Nvidia’s annual report does not name Huang as a key person. It says the company depends heavily on its longstanding executive team.
“Failure to ensure effective succession planning, transfer of knowledge, and smooth transitions involving executives and key employees could hinder our strategic planning, execution, and long-term success,” the filing says.
One man at the centre
Huang is Nvidia’s co-founder, chief executive and president. He has 33 direct reports this week, according to internal records reviewed by CNBC. He told CNBC in September 2025 that he had as many as 60. The proxy says the senior managers who work directly with him give the board a pool of candidates for promotion.
Huang owned 3.58% of Nvidia in March, the proxy shows, and he has no special voting rights, the Financial Times reported. He told Bloomberg he hoped the next chief executive already worked at Nvidia. In January, he said a chief executive who does not do the job “is let go”, the Times reported. He added a second thought.
“There will never be one like me, and the reason for that is because I was raised by the company,” Huang said.
The family at Nvidia
Three relatives work at Nvidia. His son Spencer is a director of product management in robotics, and his daughter Madison is a senior director of product marketing, according to the Times. His son-in-law, Nico Caprez, works on business development, the Times reported. Fortune gives his title as vice president of global AI infrastructure growth.
Nvidia paid Madison about $1.23m and Spencer about $1.32m in its 2026 financial year, the proxy shows. Neither is an executive officer, shares a household with Huang or reports directly to him. Their pay was set under the company’s normal practices without Huang’s involvement, the filing says.
Asked last month whether Madison was in line to succeed him, Huang said he did not wish the job on her. She cancelled a trip to Seoul on Monday, citing a “family matter”, according to Bloomberg. Huang asked for privacy for them in his memo to staff.
“My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy,” he wrote.
Nvidia reports its third-quarter results on 17 November. A day later, House committee chairs expect Huang at a closed-door briefing on Megaspeed.

articles.title: Sundrop turns your endless baby photos into recaps, time lapses, and more — without AI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
New parents take a lot of pictures of their children, but those photos often end up languishing in photo galleries, never to be seen again after the initial snap and share.
A new app, Sundrop, aims to make those pictures more useful by turning them into weekly recaps, highlights, time lapses of the child growing up, and other cute scenes, like putting the child’s photo on a magazine cover or a rookie card.
While Google Photos and Apple Photos already provide extensive tools to organize and manage photos, Sundrop is taking aim at a particular niche: parents with a new baby (usually their first!) who take an overwhelming number of photos and want to do more with those pictures.
The app was developed over the past few months by the same team behind the read-it-later app, Matter: Ben Springwater, Sky Lan, and Rob Mackenzie (all dads themselves).
Notably, Sundrop claims it is designed to be private, and processes all photos locally on the device it is installed on. To make this possible, Sundrop taps into Apple’s Vision framework and on-device Core ML (machine learning) models instead of uploading photos to a cloud server or some other hosted AI service.
Both of the child’s parents can use Sundrop together by linking their accounts, which allows the app to sync their shared photos via Apple’s iCloud service. This feature, the company says, means the pictures aren’t sent to any external servers it runs.
In addition, the team notes that no generative AI is used in the creation of its scenes or highlights.
This differentiates it from many photo-editing apps on the market, including Google’s, which are increasingly tapping generative AI to create new versions of your photos.
To find highlights and recaps, Sundrop scans pictures in the parents’ respective Camera Rolls on their iPhones, skipping things like screenshots or duplicates. It then creates highlights or fun scenes, which it calls “drops.”
One of these is a recap of the week every Sunday, announced as a Lock Screen notification. Others can put two siblings side-by-side at the same age, generate a time-lapse series of photos or a video of a kid growing up, or cut out a photo of the child and place it into a layered template.
Parents can also manually edit the photos Sundrop uses to make its creations, or use the app to automatically organize the best photos into galleries with other similar shots.
The app costs $39.99 per year, and offers a week-long free trial. The annual plan also includes Family Sharing, so only one parent needs to purchase it.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 10/11: Thế giới giảm sâu, trong nước sắp điều chỉnh
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Giá dầu quốc tế trong phiên giao dịch đầu tuần (9/11) giảm mạnh, giá dầu Brent về sát 90 USD/thùng.
Chốt phiên giao dịch 9/11, theo Reuters, giá dầu Brent giảm 5,85%, xuống còn 92,57 USD/thùng. Còn giá dầu WTI hạ 4,38%, chốt phiên ở mức 86,85 USD/thùng.
Đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay (10/11), giá dầu WTI tiếp tục đi xuống.
Theo dữ liệu từ Oilprice, vào lúc 6h22' ngày 10/11 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent vẫn được niêm yết ở mức 92,57 USD/thùng. Trong khi giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh xuống mức 86,22 USD/thùng, giảm 0,73% so với phiên liền trước.
Giá dầu Brent trong phiên 10/11 đã giảm xuống mức thấp nhất kể từ cuối tháng 8. Trong tuần trước, mặt hàng này đã "bốc hơi" 17% giá trị, ghi nhận mức giảm hàng tuần mạnh nhất kể từ khi đại dịch Covid-19 bùng phát.
Giá dầu thế giới giảm mạnh sau khi Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump phát tín hiệu hạn chế các cuộc không kích nhằm vào Iran.
Ngày 8/11, ông Donald Trump cho biết khả năng Washington tiến hành các đợt không kích mới nhằm vào Iran là “rất thấp” nếu các cuộc đàm phán đạt tiến triển.
Trước đó, ông Donald Trump từng đề cập đến khả năng nối lại các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào Iran sau cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ tại Mỹ. Còn phía Tehran tuyên bố sẽ đáp trả bằng các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào mục tiêu của Mỹ và Israel nếu bị tấn công.
Vào ngày 9/11, ông Donald Trump đã gặp Thủ tướng Qatar Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani tại Nhà Trắng. Qatar hiện đóng vai trò là trung gian, chuyển tải các đề xuất giữa Washington và Tehran nhằm thu hẹp bất đồng về chương trình hạt nhân của Iran và điều kiện chấm dứt xung đột.
Theo giới phân tích, nếu căng thẳng hạ nhiệt, hoạt động vận chuyển dầu qua eo biển Hormuz có thể được khôi phục ổn định hơn, qua đó giảm nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung và hạ nhiệt giá năng lượng toàn cầu.
Bên cạnh tác động từ yếu tố địa chính trị, giá dầu thế giới còn chịu sức ép từ triển vọng cung - cầu.
Báo cáo ngày 9/11 của Morgan Stanley chỉ ra rằng, giá dầu Brent giao ngay đã giảm xuống mức chiết khấu so với hợp đồng tương lai, phản ánh nhu cầu trên thị trường dầu vật chất có dấu hiệu chững lại.
Các nhà phân tích nhận định thị trường dầu mỏ toàn cầu đang có dấu hiệu quay trở lại tình trạng dư cung do nhu cầu suy yếu.
Theo báo cáo được công bố mới đây của ngân hàng JPMorgan, ước tính mức dư thừa dầu vào khoảng 1,4 triệu thùng/ngày trong tháng 10/2026.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Theo kế hoạch, liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính sẽ tiến hành điều chỉnh giá xăng dầu trong nước vào chiều thứ Năm (ngày 12/11).
Giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (10/11) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo kỳ điều hành ngày 5/11, giá bán lẻ tối đa của xăng E5RON92 giảm 2.305 đồng/lít, từ 23.203 đồng/lít xuống 20.898 đồng/lít.
Giá xăng E10RON95-III cũng hạ 2.075 đồng/lít, từ 23.231 đồng/lít xuống còn 21.156 đồng/lít.
Tương tự, giá dầu diesel 0.05S giảm 180 đồng/lít, từ 28.876 đồng/lít xuống còn 28.696 đồng/lít.
Trong khi giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S hạ 1.969 đồng/kg, từ 23.974 đồng/kg xuống còn 22.005 đồng/kg.
Dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương cho thấy, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam hiện ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp với diễn biến thị trường và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: Apple bán gói AI giá 1,29 triệu đồng, nhưng không phải như bạn nghĩ
articles.text:
Gói đầu tiên chỉ có trong ứng dụng làm nhạc Logic Pro, trong khi mức giá cho Siri vẫn là ẩn số.
Apple vừa bắt đầu bán thêm lượt dùng AI, lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử các tính năng Apple Intelligence vốn miễn phí. Logic Pro 13 lên Mac App Store từ ngày 5/11 với nút "Buy More Usage". Bấm vào, người dùng được mời mua "intelligence usage pack" giá 49,99 USD, khoảng 1,29 triệu đồng. Đến ngày 9/11, trang tin 9to5Mac mới phát hiện ra tùy chọn này.
Gói này thực chất là gì
Cách đặt tên dễ gây hiểu nhầm. Đây không phải thuê bao AI hàng tháng. Gói là khoản mua một lần, và người mua phải đang đăng ký Apple Creator Studio, dịch vụ trả phí 12,99 USD mỗi tháng (khoảng 335.000 đồng) hoặc 129 USD mỗi năm (khoảng 3,3 triệu đồng). Mỗi tháng, thuê bao có sẵn một mức dùng AI. Chỉ khi dùng hết mức này, lượt trong gói mới bắt đầu bị trừ.
Lượt chưa dùng hết sẽ hết hạn sau 12 tháng. Mọi giao dịch đều không hoàn tiền, trừ khi luật địa phương bắt buộc. Gói gắn với đúng tài khoản Apple đã mua nên không dùng chung qua Chia sẻ trong gia đình, dù bản thân Creator Studio chia được cho tối đa năm người. Cả nhà dùng chung một gói đăng ký thì ai hết lượt người đó phải tự mua.
Hiện chỉ Logic Pro bán gói này, dành cho trợ lý AI giúp dựng bản nhạc, thiết lập kênh thu giọng hát hay trả lời cách dùng phần mềm. Theo tài liệu của Apple, trợ lý này chạy bằng mô hình Gemini của Google, không phải mô hình do Apple tự phát triển. Keynote, Pages, Numbers, Final Cut Pro và Pixelmator Pro cũng sắp có tính năng AI trong tháng 11, và giới theo dõi Apple dự đoán các ứng dụng này sẽ bán gói tương tự.
Vì sao Apple chịu tính tiền
Lý do nằm ở chi phí. Giám đốc tài chính Kevan Parekh cho biết khi AI chạy trực tiếp trên iPhone thì rất hiệu quả, còn khi chạy trên máy chủ thì Apple phải gánh chi phí suy luận (inference), tức tiền điện và máy chủ cho mỗi lượt người dùng hỏi. Quý tới, Apple dự kiến biên lợi nhuận gộp toàn công ty giảm còn 45% đến 46%, chủ yếu vì giá bộ nhớ tăng. Trong khi đó, mảng dịch vụ đạt 31,6 tỷ USD doanh thu quý vừa rồi với biên lợi nhuận gộp 76%. Tính tiền theo lượt dùng giúp Apple không để một phần nhỏ người dùng nặng đốt chi phí của cả hệ thống.
So với ChatGPT, Gemini và Claude
Điểm khác biệt nằm ở cách tính tiền chứ không chỉ con số. Các dịch vụ AI phổ biến bán theo thuê bao hàng tháng, trong đó gói tiêu chuẩn của ChatGPT, Claude và Google đều quanh mức 20 USD (khoảng 516.000 đồng). Khi cần dùng nhiều hơn, người dùng nhảy lên bậc cao hơn. Apple chọn cách ngược lại: giữ thuê bao nền, rồi bán lượt dùng thêm theo gói nạp.
| Gói | Giá | Cách tính | 
|---|---|---|
| Gói dùng thêm AI của Apple (Logic Pro) | 49,99 USD (khoảng 1,29 triệu đồng) | Mua một lần, hết hạn sau 12 tháng, không chia sẻ gia đình | 
| Apple Creator Studio (điều kiện bắt buộc) | 12,99 USD/tháng (khoảng 335.000 đồng) | Thuê bao | 
| ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro, Google AI Pro | Khoảng 20 USD/tháng (khoảng 516.000 đồng) | Thuê bao, chatbot đa năng | 
| Gói dùng nặng của ChatGPT, Claude, Google | 100 đến 200 USD/tháng (khoảng 2,6 đến 5,2 triệu đồng) | Thuê bao, mức dùng gấp nhiều lần gói chuẩn | 
Hai bên không so sánh trực tiếp được. Gói của Apple chỉ kéo dài lượt dùng một trợ lý trong một ứng dụng cụ thể, còn khoản 20 USD kia mua quyền dùng một chatbot dùng được mọi việc. Gói 49,99 USD gần bằng bốn tháng Creator Studio và khoảng 40% gói năm. Nó cũng đúng bằng giá mua đứt Pixelmator Pro trên Mac. Apple cũng chọn cách thu tiền khác biệt: thay vì thêm một khoản thuê bao, người dùng trả một lần cho lượt dùng có thời hạn, giống nạp thẻ điện thoại hơn là đóng phí hàng tháng.
Những điều Apple chưa nói
Trang hỗ trợ của Apple không cho biết 49,99 USD mua được bao nhiêu lượt dùng. Với Logic, Apple cũng không nêu mức dùng hàng tháng, chỉ nói giới hạn phụ thuộc độ phức tạp của cuộc trò chuyện. Các tính năng khác thì có số cụ thể: tối thiểu 50 ảnh tạo ra, 250 hình, 50 bài thuyết trình Keynote hoặc ghi chú trình bày cho 700 slide mỗi tháng, mỗi con số tính khi chỉ dùng riêng tính năng đó. Người dùng Logic nặng xem được lịch sử dùng nhưng không đoán trước được một gói đủ cho bao nhiêu phiên làm việc.
Trợ lý này còn nhiều điều kiện: cần Mac chip Apple silicon chạy macOS 27, tài khoản iCloud đang hoạt động, chỉ hỗ trợ tiếng Anh Mỹ và vẫn mang nhãn thử nghiệm. Gói dùng thêm hiện chỉ bán ở tám nước là Mỹ, Canada, Anh, Pháp, Đức, Brazil, Mexico và Ấn Độ. Việt Nam không có tên trong danh sách.
Còn Siri thì sao
Đây mới là câu hỏi lớn. Apple đã nói từ tháng 9 rằng các tính năng cần mô hình trên máy chủ, gồm Siri AI, công cụ chỉnh ảnh thông minh và Image Playground, có giới hạn dùng hằng ngày. Phần dùng thêm "sẽ có phí trong tương lai". Ngày 2/11, CEO John Ternus nhắc lại điều này trên cuộc gọi báo cáo tài chính, nhưng Apple chưa công bố mức giá, mức giới hạn hay ngày áp dụng.
Thông điệp của Apple cũng chưa nhất quán. Hồi tháng 6, Apple nói quyền dùng thêm có trong "hầu hết" gói iCloud+. Đến tháng 9, tài liệu hỗ trợ chỉ nói có phí, không nhắc iCloud+. Theo MacRumors, Apple xác nhận quyền dùng thêm sẽ nằm trong một số gói iCloud+. Vì trợ lý Logic chạy bằng Gemini nên nhiều khả năng không thuộc nhóm này, nghĩa là gói 49,99 USD và iCloud+ sẽ là hai hướng thu tiền khác nhau.
Một khảo sát của CNET và YouGov năm 2025 cho thấy một nửa chủ điện thoại tại Mỹ không muốn trả thêm tiền cho AI. Apple sẽ phải thuyết phục được nhóm này khi giá cho Siri được công bố.
Trước mắt, Apple dự kiến đưa các tính năng AI còn lại của Creator Studio lên trong tháng 11. Gói dùng thêm cho Siri chưa có ngày công bố.

articles.title: Sony cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
articles.text:
Sony has canceled Fairgames, a heist game announced in 2023, according to Bloomberg. Fairgames had once been part of Sony’s big planned push for PlayStation live service games, but the company ended up canceling some planned live service titles, including in the God of War and The Last of Us franchises, and it shut down Concord shortly after its failed launch.
Sony cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
Fairgames is PlayStation’s latest cancellation as it steps back from many of its live service efforts.
The Fairgames cancellation won’t result in job cuts, and developer Haven Studios will now support other PlayStation studios, Bloomberg reports. The game was canceled following a recent test where “player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” according to part of an executive memo published by Bloomberg, which also cited “challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre.” Sony acquired Haven Studios in 2022.
Sony’s live service efforts have seen some success with Helldivers 2, which is also available on Xbox. Bungie’s Marathon, which launched this year, has had a rough start, but today the studio showed off some new features coming in a December update, including a new co-op PvE roguelite mode and a PvP deathmatch mode. Sony is also working on a live service Horizon spinoff, but recently rebooted it.

articles.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is now widely available around the world - Engadget
articles.text:
Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is now widely available around the world
The company says it can be used for the most complex tasks, such as multi-step coding and scientific research.
Google is making Gemini 4 Carbon accessible to more users after its initial release to select cybersecurity defense companies in late October. Gemini 4 Carbon promises a significant leap in AI coding and cybersecurity, as well as in scientific research. The company said that for most ordinary and even majority of software engineering tasks, Gemini 4 Argon still remains the better choice. Argon was the first Gemini 4 model and is considered less advanced than Carbon. Meanwhile, since Carbon was designed to test the limits of a model's intelligence, it's best used for multi-step coding, scientific research and discovery, as well as other more complex tasks.
The company said that Carbon had helped its first users uncover zero-day vulnerabilities in a short span of time. It has also made advances in protein structure prediction, which is necessary for developing medications. Google is giving 10,000 scientists free access to Carbon for six months to help with their research — an initiative, which would presumably help train its models in turn — and has already onboarded thousands.
Gemini 4 Carbon is now available in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business. Google AI Ultra subscribers paying $100 a month for membership will also get access to Carbon within the Gemini app, AI Model in Search and Antigravity, Google's agentic software development and AI coding platform.

articles.title: Mercedes' US fast-charging network hits 100 sites in three years
articles.text:
Mercedes-Benz’s US fast-charging network has reached 100 sites and nearly 1,000 ports in three years, with more than 550,000 sessions. The milestone comes a week after Mercedes sold its 47 European charging hubs to France’s Electra.
Mercedes-Benz’s fast-charging network in North America has reached 100 sites three years after opening its first station, InsideEVs reported. The milestone comes a week after the carmaker sold its European network.
The network now has nearly 1,000 charging points across 28 US states and British Columbia, all able to deliver up to 400 kW. Mercedes says they have handled more than 550,000 sessions for over 245,000 drivers since November 2023. Almost every site has both the older CCS plug and Tesla’s NACS plug, now standard on most new EVs.
Mercedes says its chargers are almost never down. It now focuses on how often a session starts at the first try, which rose from about 84% in 2023 to more than 90%.
Charging costs $0.35 to $0.60 per kWh, depending on the site, which are often near upmarket shopping centres. The largest, in Orlando, Florida, has 20 stalls.
Europe has gone the other way. Last week, Mercedes handed its 47 European charging hubs to French operator Electra, calling the business outside its core, Electrive reported. The US network stays “for the time being.”
Mercedes is also one of eight carmakers behind IONNA, a separate US charging network that has passed 180 sites. The US now has more than 80,000 fast-charging ports in total. US EV sales, meanwhile, remain about 40% below last year’s levels.

articles.title: Apple TV makes sign language interpretation a built-in accessibility feature | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple TV is making its content more accessible to Deaf audiences with the launch of a new Sign Language Interpretation feature, the company announced on Tuesday. The feature will initially be available across a limited set of titles, starting this Friday with the release of “Being Heumann,” a biopic about disability rights activist Judy Heumann.
American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) will also be made available for Apple’s hit movie “F1.” Later this year, other titles will follow, including “Way of the Warrior Kid” and “Greyhound.”
What makes Apple’s offering different from other platforms is that the sign language version of the film is not a separate product — that is, it’s not a separate film designed just for Deaf viewers. Instead, Apple’s support for sign language is just a setting you enable that’s integrated with the main title, similar to how you could turn on or off closed captions.
When a title with the sign language option is playing, an interpreter appears in the bottom right of the screen, translating the spoken words into signs. Apple says it has partnered with a group of DASLs (Directors of Artistic Sign Language) to ensure that the interpreter for each film fits the tone of the film. Notably, the company is not using any AI-generated interpreters, as Apple says that’s not what the Deaf community has said it needs.
The feature is shipping in the latest release of iOS 27.2, and can be turned on through a new sign language option in Settings. After being enabled, a new button will appear in the supported Apple Original titles on Apple TV indicating that sign language is available.
These titles are labeled with a sign language icon that appears on the title page alongside other features like closed captions or audio descriptions. There’s also a new section under languages that will list the specific sign languages that are available with the given title.
To make the titles more discoverable, Apple TV will highlight which titles include the sign language option in a “Movies & Shows with American Sign Language” editorial collection. Meanwhile, users can easily surface supported titles via search by typing in keywords like “with ASL,” for example.
The new feature builds on Apple’s other investments in accessibility features, which it builds itself.
“At Apple, we believe everyone should be able to enjoy great stories and entertainment,” said Sarah Herrlinger, Apple’s senior director of Global Accessibility Policy and Initiatives, in a statement about the launch. “Bringing sign language interpretation to Apple TV is an exciting step forward in making the viewing experience more accessible and inclusive for Deaf audiences. Accessibility is a core value at Apple, and we’re proud to continue creating experiences that allow more people to enjoy the content they love,” she added.

articles.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
articles.text:
Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself.
Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code.
More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities.
Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming for people to describe the characteristics of software they wanted to prove, turn these summaries into formulas, and then develop the proof. Agentic AI can significantly cut down the time of the latter project, enabling analyses like DeepMind's Signal evaluation. But even this analysis was limited in scope—it did not, for example, formally verify the entire Signal mobile app—and DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process.
“We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that,” Swarat Chaudhuri, a DeepMind research scientist, tells WIRED.
The DeepMind analysis did not find any new vulnerabilities in the portions of the Signal protocol it looked at, but when the researchers used AlphaProof Code on older versions of Signal that contain known and long-fixed vulnerabilities, it correctly identified them and showed that the protocol could not be formally verified. The researchers are releasing the specification and proof they developed for the Signal protocol analysis to aid other formal verification work.
While the speed of the project was notable, the DeepMind researchers point out that they were able to get a head start to a degree because of some past formal verification work that the Signal Foundation has conducted.
“While prior formal verification focused on smaller portions of the code, Google DeepMind's approach enables significant expansion,” Ehren Kret, Signal's chief technology officer, says in a statement. “As AI-driven security threats grow, rigorously verifying the Signal protocol implementation gives us even greater confidence in our code's privacy guarantees.”
For critical services used in high-stakes settings, it would be a dream to be able to formally verify every code base and entire software supply chains. “If you can now verify the correctness of these implementations, then you can rest easy,” says Pushmeet Kohli, chief scientist at Google Cloud and DeepMind's vice president of research. “You can imagine banks, imagine all those other companies who rely on assurances and who worry about bugs who could now say, ‘I can prove these properties.’"
The open question across the tech sector, though, is whether AI-automated formal verification can truly scale—and whether it can do so at a workable cost. DeepMind conducted the Signal analysis free of charge as a research project, and Google declined to share the cost of the analysis. The company also declined to comment on whether it has plans to release a commercial formal verification product or service.
The researchers say that some of their crucial advancements are in developing a “human-AI collaboration process,” as Chaudhuri puts it, that allows agents to contribute and self-correct at almost every phase of the process while still seeking human input and review at key junctures. “We don’t want this sort of vibe world where AI is generating the goals and AI is generating the proofs and basically taking tests that are self-written," Chaudhuri says. “There’s a middle ground.”

articles.title: Nhiều ngân hàng tăng cho vay kinh doanh bất động sản, Techcombank ngược chiều
articles.text:
Nhiều ngân hàng tăng cho vay kinh doanh bất động sản
Theo báo cáo tài chính riêng lẻ quý III/2026 của các ngân hàng niêm yết, chỉ có 12 ngân hàng công bố chi tiết dư nợ cho vay theo ngành.
Theo báo cáo tài chính quý III/2026, Techcombank là ngân hàng duy nhất trong nhóm khảo sát ghi nhận dư nợ cho vay hoạt động kinh doanh bất động sản giảm so với đầu năm.
Tại ngày 30/9/2026, dư nợ cho vay hoạt động kinh doanh bất động sản tại Techcombank đạt khoảng 204.383 tỷ đồng, chiếm 25,12% tổng dư nợ cho vay tại cùng thời điểm. Cuối năm 2025, con số tương ứng là khoảng 207.000 tỷ đồng, chiếm 28,6%.
Như vậy, sau 9 tháng, dư nợ cho vay kinh doanh bất động sản tại Techcombank giảm khoảng 2.600 tỷ đồng, trong khi tỷ trọng trong tổng dư nợ giảm 3,48 điểm phần trăm.
Ngoài Techcombank, 11 ngân hàng còn lại đều ghi nhận mức tăng về dư nợ cho vay bất động sản, tính theo giá trị tuyệt đối. Tuy nhiên, không phải ngân hàng nào cũng tăng tỷ trọng cho vay kinh doanh bất động sản trên tổng dư nợ.
Theo tỷ trọng dư nợ cho vay bất động sản/tổng dư nợ, các ngân hàng có báo cáo chi tiết dư nợ cho vay bất động sản, theo thứ tự ngân hàng có tỷ trọng cho vay bất động sản lớn nhất, bao gồm: SHB 34,11%, BVBank 31%, VPBank 25,27%, Techcombank 25,12%, TPBank 16,05%, MB 14,56%, MSB 13,53%, HDBank 12,74%, PGBank 10,26%, VIB 7,58%, LPBank 3,47%, ACB 2,48%.
Trong đó, một nửa số ngân hàng trong nhóm khảo sát ghi nhận tỷ trọng cho vay kinh doanh bất động sản tăng trong 9 tháng đầu năm, gồm BVBank, VPBank, TPBank, MB, VIB, ACB. Đáng kể nhất là TPBank tăng từ 10,6% lên 16,05%; MB tăng từ 11,37% lên 14,56%, VPBank tăng từ 23,57% lên 25,27%...
Tính chung, tổng dư nợ cho vay hoạt động kinh doanh bất động sản tại 12 ngân hàng được khảo sát đạt khoảng 1,15 triệu tỷ đồng vào cuối tháng 9/2026, tăng gần 22% so với cuối năm 2025.
Tuy nhiên, đây chỉ là số liệu của nhóm ngân hàng có công bố chi tiết dư nợ theo ngành nghề, chưa phản ánh đầy đủ quy mô và diễn biến tín dụng bất động sản trên toàn hệ thống ngân hàng.
Lãi suất vay mua nhà lên 15%, nợ xấu có thể lộ diện rõ hơn
Theo SSI Research, mặt bằng lãi suất vẫn ở mức cao, gây áp lực lên khả năng trả nợ của khu vực doanh nghiệp nhỏ và siêu nhỏ, hộ gia đình và khách hàng cá nhân. Đặc biệt, SSI Research cho rằng nợ xấu từ cho vay mua nhà sẽ lộ diện rõ hơn, làm tăng gánh nặng trích lập dự phòng của các ngân hàng trong các quý tới.
Phân tích của SSI Research cho thấy tín dụng tại các ngân hàng trong danh mục theo dõi (gồm 13 ngân hàng niêm yết hàng đầu) tăng 12,8% so với đầu năm tính đến cuối quý III/2026.
Thay đổi đáng chú ý nhất trong quý III/2026 là cơ cấu cho vay. Trong quý II, nhóm chủ đầu tư bất động sản chiếm khoảng 44% tín dụng mới tại các ngân hàng được khảo sát. Tuy nhiên, sang quý III, dư nợ cho vay nhóm này gần như đi ngang, giảm 0,2% so với quý trước. Một số ngân hàng đã thu hẹp dư nợ cho vay bất động sản, như Techcombank (-5,4%), VPBank (-1,6%), MSB (-5,7%) và VIB (-6,4%).
Ở chiều ngược lại, tín dụng vào lĩnh vực xây dựng tăng mạnh, với dư nợ tăng 17% so với quý trước và 40,4% so với đầu năm, chiếm khoảng 24% tín dụng mới. Theo SSI Research, diễn biến này cho thấy dòng vốn đang dịch chuyển dọc chuỗi giá trị bất động sản, từ hoạt động của chủ đầu tư sang giai đoạn triển khai dự án và phát triển hạ tầng.
Tốc độ dịch chuyển khác nhau giữa các ngân hàng tùy thuộc vào vị trí của từng ngân hàng trong chu kỳ dự án.
Trong đó, Techcombank dẫn đầu khi dư nợ cho vay xây dựng tăng 50% so với quý trước và tăng 140% so với đầu năm, đồng thời cắt giảm cho vay chủ đầu tư bất động sản, cho vay mua nhà và dịch vụ tài chính.
MB và HDBank duy trì cơ cấu cân bằng, tăng trưởng cả cho vay chủ đầu tư bất động sản (lần lượt tăng 7,3% và 9,5% so với quý trước) và xây dựng (lần lượt tăng 9,1% và 17,8%).
Trong khi đó, TPBank đi ngược xu hướng khi ngân hàng tăng cho vay chủ đầu tư bất động sản (tăng 6,7% so với quý trước, tăng 64,9% so với đầu năm) trong khi thu hẹp dư nợ xây dựng (giảm 7,9%), thương mại (giảm 7,6%) và bán lẻ (giảm 1,3%).
Cho vay mua nhà tiếp tục chậm lại khi chỉ tăng 1,3% so với quý trước và tăng 7,2% so với đầu năm. Trong đó, ACB tăng 2,7%, VPBank tăng 2,8%, còn Techcombank đi ngang.
Theo SSI Research, lãi suất thả nổi cho vay mua nhà ở mức 12-15%/năm và nguồn cung nhà ở vừa túi tiền hạn chế tiếp tục kìm hãm nhu cầu của người mua để ở.
Chất lượng tài sản tiếp tục suy giảm trong quý III, khi áp lực dịch chuyển sang nhóm ngân hàng TMCP quy mô vừa và nhỏ. Tỷ lệ nợ xấu toàn ngành tăng lên 2,09% trong quý III/2026, từ mức 1,97% trong quý II/2026.
Mức tăng nợ xấu tập trung tại nhóm ngân hàng TMCP với tỷ lệ nợ xấu đạt 2,83% (tăng 19 điểm cơ bản so với quý trước), dẫn đầu bởi HDBank (tăng 63 điểm cơ bản), OCB (tăng 49 điểm cơ bản), VIB (tăng 28 điểm cơ bản), TPBank (tăng 25 điểm cơ bản) và MB (tăng 22 điểm cơ bản).
Nợ xấu tại nhóm ngân hàng Big4 nhìn chung ổn định khi chỉ tăng 4 điểm cơ bản, trong khi Sacombank và VPBank ghi nhận tỷ lệ nợ xấu giảm. Nguyên nhân chính là lãi suất tăng mạnh, làm suy yếu khả năng trả nợ của người vay, đặc biệt là khách hàng cá nhân, hộ gia đình, doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa, doanh nghiệp siêu nhỏ.
SSI Research cho biết phần lớn các khoản vay mua nhà trong phạm vi phân tích có thể được điều chỉnh lãi suất lên 12-15%/năm từ quý III/2026. Do đó, nợ xấu cho vay mua nhà nhiều khả năng sẽ lộ diện rõ hơn trong các quý tới, gây thêm áp lực lên chi phí dự phòng của các ngân hàng.

articles.title: The PlayStation Plus PC app is shutting down next month
articles.text:
Sony is retiring the PlayStation Plus app for PC on December 10th. Sony says it will notify users directly about the shutdown. The app allowed PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers to stream certain games on PC, but according to Sony, not many people are using that perk:
The PlayStation Plus PC app is shutting down next month
Sony said less than 0.4 percent of PlayStation Plus Premium members were using the PC app.
With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available.
PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers can still stream games on a console or on the PlayStation Portal. Sony’s decision to take the PC app offline follows reports earlier this year saying Sony is pulling back from PC and no longer plans to release PC ports of PlayStation exclusives.

articles.title: Why does your phone keep switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data? - Engadget
articles.text:
Why does your phone keep switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data?
From weak signals to network settings, several factors can trigger the switch.
It can be annoying when your FaceTime is interrupted because your phone decided to switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data mid-call. But in truth, your device was simply doing what it thought best to keep your internet connection stable. So your phone moving from Wi-Fi to mobile data is usually a sign that something went wrong with your Wi-Fi connection.
Smartphones are designed to stay connected one way or the other. So, behind the scenes, your device is constantly measuring things like signal strength, data speed (throughput), network latency, and packet delivery. Your phone also knows which networks perform the best and where. It uses this data to make real-time decisions on when to switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data. This switch usually goes unnoticed and spares you from dropped connections and buffering screens. But the switch isn't always smooth, leading to the exact thing your device tried to avoid.
Automatic switching is meant to keep you connected, but it can come at the cost of quietly burning through your data plan or interrupting some processes that only work on Wi-Fi. A number of things can trigger your phone to switch, including a weak Wi-Fi signal, Wi-Fi connected with no internet access, and even your phone's settings. And yes, you can stop your phone from doing this, but it could lead to a worse overall experience for you.
What triggers an automatic switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data?
Your phone may switch to mobile data when the Wi-Fi signal becomes too weak, often because you're out of range or something is interfering with the connection. Different Wi-Fi bands have different ranges. The 2.4GHz band has the longest range, reaching roughly 150 to 300 feet, and penetrates walls and objects more easily. The 5GHz band is faster, but it has a shorter range of around 100 to 150 feet. It also doesn't pass through walls and objects well. The newer 6GHz band is the fastest, but its range is also the shortest, alongside poor object penetration.
Another common reason your phone switches to mobile data is when the Wi-Fi network has no access to the internet. Your internet service provider (ISP) isn't the only thing that can affect your Wi-Fi's internet access; sometimes the culprit can be network congestion, or even your router malfunctioning. Also, most phones have automatic switching features that can be turned on or off in settings. These settings affect how and when your phone switches to mobile data. An example is Connectivity Assist on iOS 27, which uses mobile data alongside your Wi-Fi connection to keep your internet connection stable.
You don't have to guess to find out the reason your phone keeps switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data; simply start with where it happens. If your iPhone or Android shows a no internet connection message, then your Wi-Fi network has lost access to the internet. The solution is to check your router and ISP. If the switch only happens in certain rooms, then it's a weak-signal issue. Lastly, if other devices work fine on Wi-Fi but your phone has switched, then an automatic switching feature is likely responsible.
How to stop your phone from switching to mobile data
Start by turning off the settings that allow your phone to automatically switch to mobile data. On iPhones, you'd need to turn off Connectivity Assist (on iOS 27) or Wi-Fi Assist (on iOS 26 and earlier).
Turn off Connectivity Assist by going to Settings > Wi-Fi > toggle off Connectivity Assist. To disable Wi-Fi Assist, open Settings > Cellular or Mobile Service > toggle off Wi-Fi Assist.
For Samsung Galaxy phones, open Settings > Connections > Wi-Fi > tap the three-dot menu icon > Intelligent Wi-Fi > turn off Switch to mobile data.
On Google Pixels, open Settings > Network & Internet > Internet > Wi-Fi preferences > disable Switch to mobile data automatically.
Now that you've stopped your phone from switching to mobile data, the next best move is to fix what triggers it. Starting with Wi-Fi network signal range, switch to your router's 2.4GHz connection since it has a longer range. And if that doesn't work well enough, look into extending your signal's range either through the best Wi-Fi extenders or the best Wi-Fi mesh systems.
If your Wi-Fi's connection to the internet keeps dropping, restart your router by unplugging it for at least 30 seconds, then check whether your ISP has an outage and update the router's firmware if an update is available. If you wish to allow your phone to switch to mobile data for a better connection, but also want to reduce data usage, then you can set certain apps or tasks to only use Wi-Fi. For example, on various apps, you can set things like downloads, cloud backup, and syncing to only happen when you're connected to a Wi-Fi network.

articles.title: Web Summit cancels Day 2 in Lisbon as Storm Charles hits Portugal
articles.text:
Web Summit has called off Wednesday’s programme in Lisbon because of Storm Charles. Portugal’s government advised the organisers that Day 2 should not take place. Web Summit told attendees by email on Tuesday evening that it aims to hold Day 3, on Thursday 12 November, as planned.
The government cited the risk of tidal flooding and severe disruption to public transport. It also pointed to the effect of high winds on outdoor structures, Web Summit said. The advice followed talks with the civil protection authority, ANEPC, and the Public Security Police (PSP).
“The safety and security of our attendees, staff and contractors is always our absolute priority,” the Web Summit team wrote.
Web Summit said it will keep working with the authorities and emergency services. It will contact those affected directly.
A state of alert across Portugal
Earlier on Tuesday, Lisbon mayor Carlos Moedas said “everything indicates” the event could not run on Wednesday. Stephen Conneely reported his comments for The Irish Times. Moedas said more than 60,000 people were at the venue in Parque das Nações.
The government has declared a state of alert across mainland Portugal for Wednesday, The Portugal News reported. Schools and non-essential public services will close. Lisbon is shutting its tunnels, parks, gardens and cultural venues from midnight. The weather service IPMA forecast gusts of up to 120km/h.
Web Summit runs from 9 to 12 November. Last month, it released its tech industry survey. In it, 60% of people in tech said AI had increased their workload.

articles.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google is notching up its chipmaking game as the company seeks to reduce its dependence on chips made by other companies for its cloud computing business. Google on Monday unveiled two new variants of its tensor processing units (TPUs), in-house-developed chips meant for AI workloads, that broaden its chip portfolio to additional use cases: confidential inference and more memory capacity for large workloads.
The new units, TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, are part of the company’s eighth generation of chips introduced in April this year, and build on what those chips offered, which was more inference capacity and support for large training requirements.
TPU 8tx, designed with AMD, is based on the TPU 8t chip, and is geared specifically for confidentially training and running AI models, Google said in a blog post. The chip “builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use,” the company wrote.
The chip also has a custom inferencing network that lets it run reasoning alongside training, so it can be used to distill and train small models on the fly. That ability, according to Google, could prove useful for cases where a company might want to train a model on its proprietary data without having to move the data between devices.
Meanwhile, TPU 8i Max basically combines two of the inference-focused TPU 8i chips the company launched in April, doubling the memory capacity, processing power and bandwidth, but in a single package. The result is a chip that lets AI models handle a larger range of information during queries.
The chip launch comes as hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, and even AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are working on their own lines of AI-specific semiconductors and accompanying software in order to reduce their reliance on the dominance of Nvidia.
The news also comes at a particularly vulnerable moment for Nvidia, whose CEO Jensen Huang over the weekend admitted to having an affair with someone alleged to be a Chinese spy.

articles.title: Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery
articles.text:
SpaceX announced a new version of its all-in-one satellite internet terminal that integrates a dish, Wi-Fi router, and now a battery into a single device about the size of a laptop. According to some users on X who shared screenshots of invitations to order Starlink Mini 2, the dish is priced at $999, which includes a full year of Roam Unlimited service that SpaceX values at $2,100.
Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery
The all-in-one satellite dish can now operate for over four hours without an external power source.
The Starlink Mini 2 will run for up to 4.5 hours on a full charge, SpaceX claims, but that can be expanded by hot-swapping in additional batteries that will be sold separately, or by connecting the dish to a 60W power source over USB-C.
Despite the addition of an integrated battery, the Starlink Mini 2 dish is thinner than the original Mini. SpaceX has managed to slim it down to 23.1mm thick, while the previous version of the Mini was 38.5mm. The Starlink Mini 2 is slightly heavier at around 3.5 pounds as a result of the added battery weight, but carries forward an IP67 dust- and waterproof rating so it’s still safe to use outdoors.
Preorders are now open “by invitation for select US customers,” according to the Starlink website, but “coming soon” to more customers and countries.

articles.title: Megaspeed imported $787m of Nvidia chips after the 2025 ban
articles.text:
Nvidia says it banned all sales and shipments to Megaspeed in June 2025, and that the ban is still in place, a company spokesman told The Wall Street Journal. Since then, Commerce has allowed Nvidia to send it parts and replacement components, the spokesman said.
Malaysian trade records show that Megaspeed imported at least 17,544 of Nvidia’s GB300 chips, worth about $787m, in November 2025, Mackenzie Hawkins reported for Bloomberg. Nvidia gave US officials a count of chips sold to Megaspeed through hardware partners. It was 50,000 units short, Bloomberg found. Megaspeed is still an official Nvidia Cloud Partner. TNW has not independently verified the reports.
Megaspeed is the Singapore company at the centre of the Jensen Huang affair. Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation after Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive. US officials believe she is a Chinese intelligence asset. China has denied the espionage claims.
What Nvidia told Washington
In mid-November 2025, Nvidia told Bloomberg that its inventory checks found everything where it should be. It also said it had asked the US government whether it needed to cut off Megaspeed, and was told no.
In December 2025, Nvidia told Bloomberg it had checked more warehouses that held the missing hardware. It did not say how many chips it found. Two of the eight data centre operators Nvidia told Washington it had visited said they had no Megaspeed hardware. Nvidia declined to comment on that to Bloomberg. Megaspeed’s largest landlord has since dropped it as a tenant.
About three months ago, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter told a White House official that Alice Huang was “not as important” in Megaspeed as she made out, according to a person familiar with the call. He said that, because of the bad publicity around her, Nvidia had stopped doing business with Megaspeed.
A call about Singapore
In late summer 2025, Teter called Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce under secretary in charge of chip export curbs. He asked whether Kessler’s Bureau of Industry and Security had a role in Singapore’s detention of Alice Huang. It did not, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. An Nvidia spokesperson said Teter did not know about the affair at the time.
It is unclear whether Teter made any specific requests of Kessler, according to Bloomberg. In the following weeks, bureau staff were told to route all requests of Nvidia through Kessler or get his approval. The people called that highly unusual, and unique to Nvidia. Staff were also told not to name Megaspeed or Speedmatrix, its Malaysian subsidiary, in external communications.
In late 2025, the Justice Department, which was working on the Megaspeed smuggling case with the bureau, asked it to pause. The bureau has made no progress since, despite having enough evidence to move forward, Bloomberg reported.
“BIS conducts all enforcement strictly by the book,” a bureau spokesman said.
“We work to resolve any allegations of ‘diversion’ promptly, to help government and our partners halt any would-be smugglers while serving the critical market of lawful customers that help America win worldwide,” an Nvidia spokesperson told Bloomberg.
A dinner in Singapore
In December 2023, Jensen Huang and a small group of colleagues met Alice Huang at an Italian restaurant in Singapore, according to The New York Times. She had just restructured Megaspeed. Four days after its ownership change, Nvidia named it a cloud partner, the Times reported on Tuesday.
Megaspeed went on to secure more than $4bn of Nvidia chips. In late 2024, the Commerce Department sent an official to inspect one of its data centres, where some Nvidia equipment was still packed in boxes. That year, Taiwan began monitoring Alice Huang’s trips to the island at the suggestion of the US government, a person familiar with the matter told the Times.
In 2025, Singapore barred her from leaving and questioned her in a probe into false import declarations. The investigations against her were closed for lack of evidence, the person said, but Singapore is still investigating Megaspeed. She later flew to Shanghai.
Megaspeed has categorically denied the chip diversion allegations. It told Bloomberg that Singapore’s probe ended this year with no adverse action against it. Its outreach to the US government went unanswered, it said. Nvidia and Megaspeed declined to comment to the Times. Alice Huang did not respond to the Times, and Bloomberg has been unable to reach her.
Congress turns to chip sales
Senators Jim Banks, a Republican, and Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat, urged Commerce to suspend or reconsider Nvidia’s China export licences, Bloomberg reported. Their bill would temporarily bar Nvidia from selling Chinese customers any chip more advanced than the H200. Lawmakers are negotiating to add it to the annual defence bill, which typically passes in December.
“I think we’re going to work hard to make sure that those provisions make it into the final version of the National Defense Authorization Act,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said.
Senator Richard Blumenthal wants a Senate investigation, Semafor reported. In the House, three committee chairs have asked Huang to attend a closed briefing on 18 November.
