articles.title: Nvidia's Huang tries to project 'business as usual' in return to office after affair revelation
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang walked into the chipmaker's Santa Clara, California, headquarters on Monday and conducted his regular morning meeting with top-level executives, people familiar with the meeting told CNBC.
On Sunday, Huang had disclosed an extramarital affair to employees.
Huang kicked off the closed-door gathering by addressing his infidelity and sharing how sorry he was to his staff, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. They said Huang didn't take any questions and quickly pivoted to business and top agenda items of the day.
The CEO was also in the office on Tuesday, conducting meetings just one week ahead of the company's quarterly earnings report.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
People inside the artificial intelligence chip giant said Huang tried to project "business as usual," even as the probe moved forward into his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The CEO was in a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, according to The Financial Times.
Sentiment toward Jensen Huang shifted on Sunday after the 63-year-old revealed in an email to employees that he had an affair, though he did not disclose with whom he had the relationship.
"I know an apology cannot undo what I have done," he wrote. "I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust." Nvidia's board opened an investigation and hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the probe on Tuesday.
Employees inside the firm described the mood to CNBC as "sad." One employee told CNBC that they were shocked by Jensen Huang's revelations.
People also told CNBC that longtime employees viewed Jensen Huang as an idol who could do no wrong and thought of him as a guiding light. Many employees at the company are also struggling to come to grips with the CEO's actions, the people said.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 to build graphics processing units for video game graphics. In recent years, the company has become synonymous with the AI boom, powering the technology that underpins large language models and the massive data center buildout.
A central figure in the development of every AI layer, the Nvidia CEO is also a key voice in Washington, even accompanying President Donald Trump on his trip to China in May. In September, Jensen Huang and his wife were pictured at the same table as Chinese President Xi Jinping for the White House's state dinner.
The news of the CEO's affair has drawn increased scrutiny on his continued support for more AI chip sales to China.

articles.title: Stock futures rise slightly as market tries to recover from Nvidia-led decline: Live updates
articles.text:
Stock futures rose slightly on Tuesday night following a losing session in which Nvidia, coupled with hotter-than-expected inflation data, pressured the broader market.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gained 88 points, or 0.2%. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.2%, while Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.4%.
In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 inched 0.1% higher on Wednesday. South Korea's Kospi lost 0.22%, while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 0.12%.
The Dow pulled back more than 150 points in regular trading, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite shed 0.4% and 0.7%, respectively. At the center of the decline was Nvidia. The chipmaker pulled back 5.5%, as CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy weighed on the stock for the second consecutive session.
Nvidia's two-day slide pulled the company's market cap down to around $4.07 trillion, its lowest since late March.
Equities also fell on Tuesday after the latest U.S. inflation data solidified expectations for a December Federal Reserve rate hike. The consumer price index increased by 0.4% month over month in October, topping expectations.
Expectations for a quarter-point rate increase next month rose to about 90% following the release, per the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
"Despite some technical uncertainty, higher than desired levels of inflation should keep the Fed in a stance of dissatisfaction with the degree of progress on inflation remaining lackluster, so hiking the Fed Funds policy rate in December is our and the market's base case," wrote Rick Rieder, CIO of global fixed income at BlackRock. "The question now is more of one of the extent of the hike."
Comments from Fed Governor Christopher Waller also led traders to price in greater chances of a quarter-point move.
Traders on Wednesday will keep their eyes on the artificial intelligence trade, after CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue that beat analyst expectations. The report initially sent the neocloud stock slightly higher.
The U.S. bond market will be closed on Wednesday for Veterans Day.

articles.title: Mississippi Senate: Scott Colom extends tight lead over Hyde-Smith as ballot deadlines hit
articles.text:
Democratic nominee Scott Colom added slightly to his narrow lead over incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi Senate election as two key ballot deadlines hit Tuesday.
Colom, a local district attorney, as of 4:30 p.m. ET, was ahead of Hyde-Smith by 2,607 votes, out of 953,547 votes counted, with an estimated 97% of the votes in, according to the Associated Press. That's a margin of just 0.27 percentage points.
Independent candidate Ty Pinkins had 20,034 votes.
Tuesday is the deadline for resolving affidavit or provisional ballots, which are cast by voters whose eligibility is disputed or unclear on Election Day. It is also the deadline for the receipt of mail-in absentee ballots that are postmarked by Election Day, Nov. 3.
Mississippi is one of just two states whose Senate election has not been called. Alaska is the other.
Democrats so far have flipped seven Senate seats held by Republicans going into the election. That gives Democrats a new majority in the Senate of at least 54 seats in the 100-member chamber come January.
Alaska before Election Day was viewed as possibly key to the question of whether Republicans would retain their narrow majority in the Senate.
Mississippi, which has not elected a Democratic senator since the segregationist John Stennis in 1982, was on few political analysts' radar as a possible pickup for Democrats. If Colom wins his race, he would be the first Black senator from Mississippi since the post-Civil War Reconstruction Era.
In Alaska, Democratic nominee Mary Peltola is ahead by just 2,517 votes over incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, with 218,641 total votes counted, a margin of 1.1 percentage points.
Peltola has 48.6% of the total vote. If neither she nor Sullivan gets more than 50% of the total vote, the race will go to a ranked-choice round, in which the two other candidates, Gerald Heikes and another candidate named Dan Sullivan, will be eliminated, and the second choices of voters who made them their first choice will be allocated between Peltola and the incumbent.

articles.title: CoreWeave beats on revenue and lifts guidance, easing AI slowdown concerns
articles.text:
CoreWeave reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and lifted its 2026 guidance on Tuesday, showing that demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure remains strong despite concerns of a market slowdown. The stock advanced in extended trading.
The earnings announcement lands at a particularly volatile moment for CoreWeave and its neocloud peers, as the market sours on the AI trade and as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the central figure in the global buildout, faces a scandal tied to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus:
- Loss per share: 95 cents adjusted vs. $1.16 expected
- Revenue: $3.66 billion vs. $3.55 billion expected
CoreWeave's revenue soared 168% from about $1.36 billion a year earlier, according to a statement. The company recorded a net loss of $709 million, or $1.27 per share, compared to a net loss of $110 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings exclude stock-based compensation.
Executives pushed up their forecast for 2026. They now see $1.275 billion to $1.375 billion in adjusted operating income on $13 billion to $13.3 billion in revenue. Analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha were looking for $1.07 billion in adjusted operating income, and analysts polled by LSEG had expected $12.86 billion in 2026 revenue.
In August, CoreWeave's 2026 guidance included $960 million to $1.15 billion in adjusted operating income and $12.4 billion to $13.2 billion in revenue.
CoreWeave has lost over 40% of its value in the past month, as investors rotate out of companies most closely tied to AI infrastructure. Rising interest rates have pushed lenders out of the market, raising concerns about ongoing access to capital. Some CoreWeave bond yields recently topped 16%.
"The business can execute well and still face a tougher financing environment," Joe Tigay, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, wrote in an email. "Strong demand is encouraging; the cost and availability of capital remain critical."
CoreWeave will get most the capital it needs for 2027 through clients pre-payments and financing from hardware partners, and the company will raise "a limited amount" as well, CEO Mike Intrator told analysts on a conference call.
The company plans to raise new debt tied to a set of contracts in the weeks to come, said Nitin Agrawal, its finance chief.
"At current yields, we do not intend to issue additional parent-level unsecured debt through 2027," he said. "By contrast, the asset-level secured debt market has remained stable, with our loans continuing to trade around par value." In all, he said he projects under $5 billion in parent-level debt financing through 2027.
Fellow neocloud Nebius, whose stock is down by a similar amount, is scheduled to report earnings on Thursday. Nebius shares got a small boost from CoreWeave's results.
Both companies and several other providers of cloud-based graphics processing units are particularly reliant on Nvidia, which provides GPUs as well as necessary capital to the whole ecosystem. Nvidia shares have dropped nearly 10% to start the week as the Huang affair raises pressure on the company in Washington, D.C. Nvidia's board said on Tuesday that it hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate Huang and determine whether national security or company secrets were compromised.
CoreWeave investors are also looking toward next week, when key customer Anthropic is scheduled to debut on the Nasdaq. In its updated IPO prospectus on Tuesday, Anthropic indicated that it could be valued at around $1.4 trillion after its share sale. Anthropic has signed deals for the construction of entire data centers that will meet its needs. "We see that we're going to have long-term relationships with the AI labs," said Intrator, a CoreWeave co-founder.
During the quarter, CoreWeave said it would establish its first data centers in Asia and announced the Forge service for running and evaluating AI models.
Management still anticipates 1.85 gigawatts in active power by the end of 2026. CoreWeave is targeting $37 billion to $39 billion in full-year capital expenditures, which would imply 155% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha were looking for $37.69 billion.
CoreWeave owed almost $47 billion in debt at the end of the third quarter, according to the statement. Like its bigger cloud rivals such as Amazon and Oracle, CoreWeave is rushing to bolster computing capacity for clients.
But last week, voters in the U.S., where CoreWeave derives most of its revenue, rejected dozens of initiatives on data center development. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated the incumbent, Republican Greg Abbott, after she said Abbott should try to end 20-year tax breaks on large data centers.
"So to begin with, we do not anticipate any impact from the seismic regulatory shift that's occurred," Intrator said.
Almost all of CoreWeave's power is online or is permitted and under construction, he said.
"If data center construction across the sector were to slow, installed compute becomes scarcer, and the knock-on effect is that GPU pricing may stay higher for longer," Intrator said.
He said the company does not expect risks to deliveries in 2027 based on construction at permitted locations.
"We could sell all of the capacity that we have to current buyers that are in the queue. We are choosing not to," Intrator said. We're choosing to be patient. We're choosing to bring the infrastructure to market when it is further along, because we believe that that will result in better economic output for the outstanding infrastructure that we have."
Meanwhile, demand remains robust, with the company now sitting on a $132.5 billion revenue backlog, up from $104 billion as of June.
"Should we choose to focus only on our committed backlog, we would expect capex for 2027 to remain in line with our 2026 capex investment, while revenue and EBITDA grow significantly," Agrawal said.
WATCH: Cramer's Mad Dash: CoreWeave

articles.title: Fossil CEO says turnaround is ahead of plan as sales return to growth
articles.text:
Fossil Group posted quarterly results on Tuesday that could point to early signs of a turnaround for the legacy watchmaker.
The company, which has struggled to compete with new gadgets in the years since its sales and stock price peaked in the 2010s, has been quietly undertaking a comeback strategy under CEO Franco Fogliato. The company's fiscal third-quarter earnings indicate the strategy is beginning to bear fruit.
The company said Tuesday that it returned to profitability in the third quarter, posting operating income of $25.3 million, compared with an operating loss of $21.7 million last year. It also returned to sales growth, with net sales up 0.4% to $271.2 million. The company last reported a year-over-year sales increase in the first fiscal quarter of 2022.
"We're excited about improving dramatically the profitability of the company through a very strong and disciplined management of full-price sales as well as cost management," Fogliato told CNBC in an exclusive interview.
For the quarter ended Oct. 3, Fossil reported net income of $11.7 million, or 19 cents per share, compared with a net loss of $39.9 million, or 76 cents per share, the year prior. The company also said its operating expenses fell 11.1% to $137 million. The company last posted quarterly net income in the third fiscal quarter of 2022.
With the signs of growth, the retailer also raised its full-year outlook, guiding for full-year net sales of between $980 million and $990 million, which would mark a slight decline from just over $1 billion in net sales in the prior year. That compares with a previous expectation of net sales falling between 3% and 5%. Fossil also said it's expecting positive free cash flow by the end of the year.
Fogliato said Fossil had previously not expected sales growth for another year and a half.
The stronger quarter comes after the company saw slumping sales and financial losses over the past few years. It struggled with the rise of smartwatches, mounting debt and the decline in mall foot traffic.
Fossil stock has lost the vast majority of its value since the early-to-mid 2010s, and despite a recent surge, was trading under $8 a share on Tuesday.
To rightsize the business, Fogliato, who joined Fossil in 2024, said he focused on closing stores, moving away from promotions to full-price sales, improving marketing and broadening Fossil's product range. That meant shrinking the business to a sustainable baseline before trying to grow it.
The company saw a 5.9% decrease in direct-to-consumer sales for its third quarter, which Fogliato attributed to the company's "aggressive" downsizing.
"We simplified a lot of the business doing this," Fogliato said, adding that customers responded well when the company moved away from markdowns. "People tell me they are excited about what they are seeing in the marketplace now."
Fossil added that its key growth engine for the quarter was Asia, where net sales grew 15.1%. Fogliato said much of that growth was led by the India market.
At the same time, growing internationally is only part of the watchmaker's strategy as it tries to improve its performance in its home country.
"Priority number one is to grow our home market, and we're doing that," he said. "As retail is settling into a smaller, more profitable base, ready to grow again, we're entering 2027 with plenty of opportunities."
Fogliato said one key to growth was not trying to keep up with the smartwatch trend. While trying to make gains in the smartwatch space initially hampered Fossil's performance, it's now investing in analog watches again.
Smartwatch sales came in under $1 million for the quarter, but sales for traditional watches — which make up around 86% of Fossil's sales — grew 6.4%.
"Fossil is literally having a comeback, a strong comeback, a momentum, and we can see this," Fogliato said. "And it comes not only through the numbers — it comes with the excitement we see in the stores, and we think we're just at the beginning. We have so much work to do."

articles.title: On-demand pay is giving workers earlier access to earned wages as living costs rise
articles.text:
In a world worried about the impact of artificial intelligence on jobs, the war in Iran, and an intensely polarized political landscape, ask employees what keeps them up at night and it's likely the answer will be their finances.
Financial stress has reached a breaking point for many Americans. Nine in 10 workers report that their pay is falling behind rising costs, according to the 2026 Monster Cost of Living Report. Thirty-eight percent report relying more on credit cards or loans to make ends meet, as prices for groceries, gas and other everyday expenses rise.
At the recent CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City, Nelson Chai, CEO of on-demand pay platform DailyPay, told CNBC's Sharon Epperson that workers' top priorities are not benefits like "the gym membership or pet insurance or some of those things that are things they can add on to."
"They want to get paid on time so they can take care of bills," he said.
Chai said for employers, this means more workers — especially hourly — are worried, distracted, or simply not there because they have to choose between buying food and paying bills or covering the cost of commuting to work. There are roughly 160 million frontline employees in the U.S., many of whom live paycheck to paycheck, he said.
Without access to earned wages, workers often turn to costly alternatives such as payday loans or overdraft protection, creating a "damaging cycle of debt," he added.
"The payroll system in this country was set up in 1938 and it hasn't evolved since," Chai said. On-demand pay platforms, like DailyPay, enable workers to access their earned wages when they want rather than wait for the typical bi-weekly paycheck.
"Workers need to figure out how to get to work. They need to figure out how to put food on the table. So those are the things DailyPay is really focused in on," Chai said. He said the company already has more than 2,000 companies in the U.S. as clients, including Tractor Supply, AstraZeneca, and Dollar Tree.
'Meeting workers where they are'
Employees can access their wages via DailyPay in a few different ways, Chai said. One option is to use the company's debit card; another is to do an ACH transfer; or transfer to the bank of the employee's choice. Employees pay a $3.49 flat fee only if they want instant access to their money; if not, the wait is one to three business days.
"After you've taken out what you want to take out, then we send you the remainder of pay at the time of the normal paycheck," he said. "It's about meeting the workers where they are."
Metz Culinary Management in Dallas, Pennsylvania, is a DailyPay client. Cheryl McCann, vice president of human resources for the food services company, said it's hard to recruit the servers, cooks, cashiers and housekeepers she needs, but it's even harder to keep them.
So, when she saw that an increasing number of her employees — most of whom are hourly — were asking the company to loan them money in between the biweekly pay cycle, she knew the family-run business had to do something to relieve the financial stress.
"They were coming to us asking to loan them $200 to pay a bill or keep from having their car repossessed," McCann said. And while the company didn't have the bandwidth to move to a weekly pay cycle, loaning employees money wasn't sustainable either.
When McCann saw a DailyPay booth at an ADP conference she was intrigued but skeptical. "I thought 'This could really work,' but it almost seemed too good to be true," she said.
She gathered more information, spoke to the leadership at Metz, and in 2019, rolled out the benefit, at no cost to the company. Today, McCann says 65% of Metz employees are using the DailyPay app.
"It's incredibly popular with our workers and they tell us all the time how much they appreciate it," McCann says. "One worker told us it was the first time he paid his bills on time."
Offering on-demand pay has also helped with retention, McCann says, as well as recruitment. The company highlights on-demand pay in some of its advertising and includes it in onboarding materials.
DailyPay works with employers that have a significant hourly worker labor pool, although salaried workers can access it as well. Chai said DailyPay's technology coordinates with a client's human resources tech stack making it easy to integrate. Videos and other materials to explain the benefit to employees are provided by DailyPay, something that was crucial for McCann.
"I think I sent them one file," she says. "DailyPay did everything else."
On-demand pay isn't making groceries, gas and other living expenses less expensive, but McCann said it does ease the financial stress of her employees. "They're not taking out huge amounts," she says, "but when they have the money to take their kids somewhere or pay for a flat tire, they tell us what a difference it's making in their lives."
To join the CNBC Workforce Executive Council, apply at cnbccouncils.com/wec.

articles.title: White House vows to press ahead with tariffs despite midterm backlash over rising prices
articles.text:
One week after voters punished Republicans over rising prices in the midterm elections, President Donald Trump's White House signaled it would stay the course on tariffs, even as his former top economic advisor warned that Americans are footing the bill.
Jim Goyer, Trump's director of White House Office of Public Liaison, defended tariffs as a tool to rebuild U.S. manufacturing, secure supply chains and protect national security during an address Tuesday at the B20 summit, a gathering of global business leaders in Washington hosted by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.
"And we are just getting started," Goyer said. "Our ambition is to continue this pace for the remainder of the president's term in office."
But Gary Cohn, who served as Trump's chief economic advisor during his first administration, offered a sharply different assessment during an onstage interview later Tuesday.
"Tariffs are a consumption tax on the U.S. consumer," Cohn said, arguing that the duties are raising prices and forcing Americans to reconsider purchases.
The divide exposed a growing dilemma for Trump. His trade agenda is reshaping global commerce – and driving up costs for voters. Companies are adapting to the chaos, but the old trading system isn't coming back.
"President Trump has disrupted that system in a way that we're not likely to return to," Kevin Brady, a former Republican congressman who helped lead the B20 summit, said during a discussion with U.S. Chamber CEO Suzanne Clark.
The political backlash was evident in the Nov. 3 election. Roughly two-thirds of voters said Trump's policies contributed to inflation, according to the CNBC Voter Poll. Nearly nine in 10 said the cost of living was a major or crucial factor in their vote.
A separate Reuters/Ipsos poll released Tuesday found 62% of Americans supported repealing Trump's tariffs, while just 21% approved of his handling of the cost of living.
"Last week, American voters sent a clear message about the cost of living and their economic security," Clark said in her keynote address.
The pressure intensified Tuesday as new government data showed consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, exceeding economists' expectations. Annual inflation reached 3.7% in September, the latest available year-over-year figure and well above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.
Tariffs are not the only factor driving higher prices. The war with Iran has pushed energy costs sharply higher, while housing, healthcare and other household expenses continue to strain consumers.
But research has found Trump's import duties have added to those pressures. A Federal Reserve Bank of New York study estimated that about 26% of tariff increases were passed through to consumer prices, with some effects taking nine to 12 months to work through supply chains.
Cohn, now vice chairman of IBM, argued that while tariffs generate revenue for the U.S., those gains come at consumers' expense.
"You're looking at one side of the equation. You're looking at the credit side of the balance sheet," Cohn said, describing how he would respond to Trump's defense of tariff revenue. "There's the debit side of the balance sheet, which is every hardworking American who happened to pay the tariff through some product that they bought."
Still, Cohn saw room for a bipartisan trade deal. He suggested Trump and the incoming Democratic Congress could make protections against China and unfair trade practices permanent while rolling back tariffs on Canada, leaving less for future presidents to undo.
For businesses, the shift is already underway. UPS CEO Carol Tomé said customers are moving production and sourcing closer to home as global supply chains become more regional.
"Supply chains are diversifying. Supply chains are regionalizing," Tomé said during a panel discussion moderated by CNBC's Morgan Brennan.
Separately, UPS is opening a new $80 million-plus air hub in the Philippines in October to expand its Asian network and improve connections across more than 1,100 global trade lanes.
Other executives, like Jim Fitterling, executive chairman of chemicals giant Dow, defended Trump's tariffs despite their costs. Fitterling acknowledged they can drive up prices but argued they are necessary to combat unfair competition and protect U.S. manufacturing.
Democrats plan to challenge Trump's tariffs when they take control of Congress in January, but his veto power and broad trade authority could make them difficult to overturn.

articles.title: It's time to buy the dip on this key aerospace supplier. Why the shares can rebound
articles.text: I'm a momentum trader, and I'm always looking for stocks where the potential reward outweighs the risk. Today I've got my eye on Howmet Aerospace . The Pittsburgh-based company makes some of the most critical components in jet engines and power turbines. Think: turbine blades that withstand extreme heat, along with the fasteners that hold aircraft together. Howmet supplies major aerospace manufacturers, including GE Aerospace, and has a leading position in the market for high-performance turbine components. Key points Strong third-quarter earnings showed the business is still growing rapidly, despite concerns about competition. Management raised its full-year outlook and expects more growth in 2027. Howmet is buying back billions in stock, and shares are now even cheaper. Howmet's stock has fallen roughly 30% from its August high, even after the company delivered strong earnings. Investors are worried about new competition. GE Aerospace is acquiring a rival turbine-parts supplier, while SpaceX plans to start making its own turbine blades. But I think the market is overreacting. It could take years for these moves to meaningfully threaten Howmet's business, which continues to deliver strong results today. HWM YTD mountain Howmet Aerospace, YTD Why I'm buying The company just delivered a great quarter In Howmet's third-quarter results, revenue jumped 29% from a year earlier to $2.7 billion, including 25% organic growth. Adjusted earnings per share climbed 54% to $1.46, beating Wall Street's estimate of $1.37. Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 32.5%, showing that Howmet is generating strong profitability. Those are impressive numbers for a company whose stock has been under so much pressure. Management sees more growth ahead Howmet raised fourth-quarter earnings-per-share guidance to a range of $1.49 to $1.51, compared to the consensus estimate of $1.42 from analysts. It then raised EPS guidance for the full year to a range of $5.45 to $5.51. Companies with a broken moat do not raise guidance for the quarter and for the year in the same release. Howmet is putting billions behind its own stock The company has repurchased $1.1 billion in stock so far this year. At the end of last month, the company authorized an increase its share-purchase program to $5.4 billion, up from $5 billion. Why now? I'm not dismissing the competitive threat from new suppliers, but Wall Street agrees with me that this is already priced into the stock. Analysts still see the shares rebounding by more than 35% over the next 12 months. Bottom line This crucial player in the aerospace pipeline is fundamentally strong and getting stronger. The company is investing alongside you with its robust share buyback. Steven Grasso is the CEO of Grasso Global Inc. articles.title: GE Vernova sellers have it all wrong — plus, why Fed rate hike odds are soaring
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch — an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. Markets fell broadly on Tuesday , reversing a large chunk of Monday's more than 2% gains in the S & P 500 and Nasdaq . Volatility remains elevated, with stocks flipping from one day to the next. That's why we are hesitant to chase stocks higher or turn too negative after a big downdraft. What the market is struggling to sort out is the midterm election's impact on the data center buildout and the ongoing controversy at Nvidia . We downgraded our rating on the chipmaker to a 2 on Tuesday morning because there is too much uncertainty for us to buy shares, even after a 10% decline over the past two days. The 10-year Treasury yield surged back to 5% after the October consumer prices came in hotter than expected. The CPI rose 0.4% year over year, faster than the 0.3% that economists expected. Core CPI, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, increased 0.3%, above the 0.2% forecast. No year-over-year figures were provided because last year's government shutdown prevented the release of October 2025 data. The CPI sharply raised Fed rate hike expectations at its upcoming December meeting. Not only is the market now fully pricing in a 25-basis-point increase next month, but it also puts a 12% probability on the Fed raising rates by 50 basis points, according to CME FedWatch. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller got the 50-basis-point conversation going early Tuesday, before the data was released. Waller said at an event in London that he was "leaning toward" raising rates if October's data was soft, but would support "more robust action" if the data came in hot. And that's exactly what we got. GE Vernova shares tumbled Tuesday after SoftBank took a $3.7 billion write-down tied to its power equipment strategy for AI data centers in the U.S. Included in this purchase process overhaul is SoftBank's massive Ohio data center project, for which GE Vernova is the supplier of natural gas turbines used to generate behind-the-meter energy. SoftBank said the Ohio project is on track, but the contract is being revised. It also said that Elon Musk claims last week in an X post that SoftBank was defaulting on its turbine orders is "simply not correct at all." GE Vernova told Jim Cramer: "Customers are securing slots further into the 2030s, and as we've said, we've sold slots for 2032 delivery, and we expect all slots through 2030 to be mostly sold by the end of 2026. SoftBank's announcement has no impact on that." GE Vernova said SoftBank remains a valued customer, and there is "no negative or positive financial impact" based on what the company disclosed Tuesday. In a Tuesday note to clients, JPMorgan wrote that if any delays or cancellations were to occur, GE Vernova could shift the order to waiting customers. Jim has a similar read on the situation: "If there are slots available, they're going to be taken by the end of the day." The nearly 10% decline in Club stock at its worst levels of the day was an overreaction. However, we are not rushing in to add to our data center exposure right now, considering the concerns about a slowdown in the buildout due to the Democratic wave in last week's midterm elections. By the close, GE Vernova shares pared their losses and finished down less than 4%. CoreWeave reports earnings after the close , and what the neocloud company says about compute demand, the funding environment, and the ability to build new data centers in the U.S. could influence sentiment around the AI trade. There are no major earnings before the opening bell on Wednesday. The only economic release Wednesday is weekly mortgage applications. articles.title: Rep. Jim Jordan, Sen. John Thune elected GOP leaders in Congress
articles.text:
Republican lawmakers on Tuesday picked Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio and Sen. John Thune of South Dakota to serve as their respective House and Senate minority leaders in the next Congress.
Jordan, the House Judiciary Committee chairman, was elected in a 106-73 vote, sources told MS NOW on condition of anonymity to discuss the private meeting. He beat Rep. Steve Scalise, R-La., the current House majority leader.
A two-decade House veteran and committed supporter of President Donald Trump, Jordan will take on the leadership role just as Republicans relinquish power, following blowout Democratic victories in last week's midterm election.
House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., announced the day after Election Day that he would not run for minority leader in the 120th Congress.
Thune, in a statement, said he "appreciated the opportunity to have an open, honest, and transparent conversation with my colleagues today, and I am honored to have their continued trust and support to lead the Senate Republican Conference in the 120th Congress."
"I'm proud of what this Republican team has accomplished together, and we remain united in our commitment to advancing conservative priorities, working with President Trump and our colleagues in the House, and holding the line against Democrats' efforts to enact their far-left, liberal agenda," Thune said in the statement.
"We have important work ahead of us, and I look forward to serving alongside my colleagues on behalf of the American people," he said.

articles.title: Traders bet on a pop for Anthropic's historic IPO
articles.text:
News of Anthropic's historic initial public offering provided a wave of relief for tech investors. The response in the perpetual futures market might provide even more relief.
As Anthropic prepares to raise money in its initial public offering this month, traders in offshore markets are making large bets that there will be a big pop on the AI giant's debut.
Trying to guess an initial first day IPO reaction is nearly impossible, but a new and fast-growing corner of the markets might offer some clues.
Pre-IPO perpetuals, contracts that aim to track the price of private companies, trade on decentralized crypto exchanges like Hyperliquid, Coinbase, Binance and OKX to name a few. The current Hyperliquid Anthropic contract implies a stock price of $98 and its market cap at roughly $1.7 trillion, more than 30% higher than the $70-$78 range announced in the company's updated S1.
While trading on the exchange is not currently available to American investors, about $250 million of volume traded across Hyperliquid's two Anthropic trackers in the past 24 hours, according to the exchange.
Hyperliquid's pre-IPO Anthropic perp began trading two weeks ago at $138 before settling into a roughly ten-dollar range between $110 and $120 prior to last week's selloff in tech stocks, as the contract slipped below $94 at one point.
To proponents of this new asset class, the pricing of the perps is evidence that bankers intentionally undersell equity ahead of IPOs to ensure a post-market "pop." Looking at SpaceX, the argument rings true: pre-IPO perps on SpaceX traded at a premium and converged with equity prices at the IPO, all before shares went on a three-day rally of as much as 40% in the immediate aftermath of the listing.
News of Anthropic's upcoming roadshow may be weighing on competitor OpenAI. Perps tracking OpenAI's market cap dropped 7% to $1.27 trillion, according to Hyperliquid trading on a contract trading $2.8 billion in volume over the past 24 hours.
Shares of Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR), the publicly-traded Treasury company investing in the HYPE tokens that power the exchange fell 4% Tuesday. The stock is up 150% on the year.

articles.title: Op-ed: In Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged China spy scandal, there's plenty of blame to go around
articles.text:
In June 2013, President Barack Obama welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Sunnylands, a secluded California estate, for an informal summit. Behind the diplomatic pleasantries, Obama confronted Xi over Chinese state-directed cyber-enabled espionage and theft of American intellectual property, warning that such activities threatened American companies and the broader bilateral relationship.
Thirteen years after the Sunnylands Summit, the threat has evolved significantly as the race to dominate AI frames the U.S.-China relationship. The stakes are higher, the technology more consequential, and the vulnerabilities increasingly involve attempts to compromise or coopt the "key man" at the helm of the nation's top technology companies.
With the unfolding scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the blame should start with the CEO himself, but it should not end there. The situation illustrates a failure of Silicon Valley, corporate and political leadership at a much wider level.
Huang has acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman identified in reporting as Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. American intelligence officials reportedly believe she was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information and potentially influence Nvidia's efforts to loosen American semiconductor export restrictions. China denies the allegations.
Nvidia's independent directors have launched an investigation, and so far, they say no compromise of company secrets or national security information has been established. But the problem extends well beyond Huang or Nvidia. Focusing exclusively on whether proprietary technology or trade secrets were transferred fundamentally misunderstands the potential intelligence value of such an operation.
For Beijing, gaining insight into, influencing, or potentially compromising American technology policymaking could be equally valuable. Advance knowledge of export-control deliberations, regulatory intentions, negotiating positions, or divisions within the administration could provide strategic advantages without a single semiconductor design being stolen.
The Trump administration reportedly received warnings about the relationship before the scandal became public. Nevertheless, Huang remained an influential participant in semiconductor policy discussions while advocating greater access to China's market.
New reporting also raises questions about interactions between Nvidia and Commerce Department officials during an investigation into Megaspeed, subsequently transferred to the Justice Department. No improper influence has been established, but corporate access to government decision-making deserves scrutiny alongside proprietary technology.
It is a new era of 'key man' risk with AI
Whether appropriate protective measures were taken remains unclear. President Donald Trump's public defense of Huang — saying that Huang told him he had no idea the woman could be a spy and that he trusted the CEO, and that if national intelligence had warned the president about this threat, as has been reported, he didn't remember — hardly conveyed the urgency warranted by allegations of a foreign intelligence operation targeting a strategically indispensable American company.
Trump has met Xi three times since returning to office, with two additional encounters anticipated in November and December. These meetings offer Trump an opportunity to follow Obama's example by confronting Xi directly over Chinese state-directed or sponsored espionage targeting American technology companies, their executives, and potentially the U.S. policymaking process.
It is also time for a more formal check from Congress on Silicon Valley, which has long celebrated the visionary founder, the indispensable executive whose genius supposedly transcends conventional corporate management and traditional corporate governance. Investors have rewarded this concentration of authority, while boards have all too frequently accommodated it.
Corporate governance professionals call this "Key Man" risk: excessive organizational dependence on an individual whose departure, financial misconduct, or moral compromise could materially damage the enterprise. In the artificial intelligence era, this risk becomes considerably more dangerous. When a handful of executives control technologies central to America's economic competitiveness, military capabilities, and intelligence advantages, their personal vulnerabilities become potential national security vulnerabilities.
When those executives also enjoy extraordinary access to the White House and senior policymakers, they become potential conduits for foreign intelligence collection and influence directed not simply at their companies, but at the American people and American policy itself.
How Congress can act to take back control from Silicon Valley
Congress has opportunities to strengthen America's defenses and must act immediately.
The AI OVERWATCH Act would strengthen oversight of advanced semiconductor exports and associated national security licensing conditions.
The MATCH Act would address weaknesses in restrictions on advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment, including foreign suppliers and servicing arrangements.
The Chip Security Act would strengthen mechanisms for tracking advanced chips and detecting diversion.
Importantly, the Remote Access Security Act would extend export-control authorities to certain remote access arrangements, including cloud computing, addressing the possibility that restricted American technological capabilities could be accessed without physically exporting the underlying equipment.
Together, these measures address important technological and regulatory gaps and vulnerabilities. But controlling chips, equipment, and computing access admittedly will not solve the human vulnerabilities problem — the so-called "Key Man" risks to U.S. technology supremacy and national security.
Most of these bills have a good amount of Congressional bipartisan support. However, they have encountered stiff resistance from the technology industry and their lobbyists, and some very detailed disagreements over specifics of export-control policy. There has also been uncertainty about White House support for these bills and an unwillingness by the Republican-controlled Congress to get on the wrong side of the White House. However, there is no doubt in my mind the Nvidia controversy has given supporters a new argument for action. The Democratic takeover of both chambers could further strengthen congressional oversight and an appetite for codifying much of this into law using these pieces of legislation.
There should also be a serious discussion among key U.S. government and corporate governance experts about whether strategically important technology companies need explicit board-level counterintelligence responsibilities, independent executive-security assessments, and confidential mechanisms for reporting foreign intelligence approaches to the appropriate channels.
This is not about morally policing executives' private lives. It is about recognizing that individuals controlling America's most sensitive technologies, and influencing the policies governing them, are valuable intelligence targets and assets if compromised.
Unfortunately, the Trump administration's broader philosophy appears to emphasize voluntary industry commitments and confidence in technology executives' ability to police themselves. Morality is not a governance system. Personal assurances are not counterintelligence safeguards. Importantly, shareholder interests are not always synonymous with the national interest.
Obama understood at Sunnylands that protecting American innovation required confronting China directly. That engagement helped to clearly articulate American redlines against cyber-enabled theft of intellectual property for commercial advantage.
Trump now has an opportunity, and a responsibility, to extend that principle to today's intelligence threats. At his forthcoming meetings with Xi, he should make clear that state-directed or sponsored operations targeting American technology executives and attempts to compromise U.S. technology policymaking are unacceptable and carry consequences for the bilateral relationship.
But confronting Beijing is only half the responsibility. Washington must also confront weaknesses within the body of laws governing technology access and must weigh in on America's corporate institutions and governance.
America cannot declare artificial intelligence essential to national security while leaving protection of its technology, executives, and policymaking process primarily to corporate discretion. The greatest vulnerability in Silicon Valley may not be the technology we export, but the people and governance systems entrusted to protect it, and the policies determining who gets access to it.
Neither Congress nor the White House should be comfortable leaving that responsibility to Silicon Valley's own moral code.
—By Dewardric McNeal, Managing Director and Senior Policy Analyst at Longview Global, and a CNBC Contributor. He worked in the U.S. Department of Defense as an East Asia and China security relations expert during the Obama administration.

articles.title: Ra lệnh bắt khẩn cấp nhân viên y tế trường học Phạm Hoàng Phương SN 1989
articles.text:
Ra lệnh bắt khẩn cấp nhân viên y tế trường học Phạm Hoàng Phương SN 1989
Phạm Hoàng Phương SN 1989 là đối tượng dùng dao hành hung Hiệu trưởng Trường THPT An Biên.
- 11-11-2026Thi hành lệnh bắt tạm giam nguyên quản lý siêu thị Nguyễn Công Nhạ SN 1996

- 10-11-2026Nguyên quản lý cửa hàng Bách Hóa Xanh ở An Giang tham ô hơn 1,4 tỷ tiền hàng
Ngày 10/11/2026, Công an xã An Biên cho biết Cơ quan Cảnh sát điều tra Công an tỉnh An Giang đã ra lệnh bắt khẩn cấp và tạm giữ hình sự đối với ông Phạm Hoàng Phương (sinh năm 1989, trú tại xã Vân Khánh, tỉnh An Giang) để điều tra làm rõ về hành vi “Cố ý gây thương tích”.
Trước đó, qua xác minh, vào khoảng 07 giờ 45 phút ngày 05/11/2026, Phạm Hoàng Phương, nhân viên y tế học đường Trường Trung học phổ thông An Biên, đến phòng làm việc của ông Quách Mạnh Hùng (sinh năm 1968, trú tại xã An Biên, tỉnh An Giang), là Hiệu trưởng để trao đổi về việc giải quyết đơn xin chuyển công tác.
Trong quá trình trao đổi, hai bên xảy ra tranh cãi. Phạm Hoàng Phương đã sử dụng dao (loại dao yếm, dài khoảng 40 cm) mang theo từ trước tấn công ông Quách Mạnh Hùng, gây thương tích ở vùng tay. Ngay sau khi tiếp nhận tin báo, Công an xã An Biên khẩn trương có mặt tại hiện trường, đưa Phạm Hoàng Phương về trụ sở làm việc; đồng thời phối hợp đưa người bị thương đi cấp cứu, tổ chức khám nghiệm hiện trường và thu giữ các vật chứng có liên quan.
Hiện vụ việc đang tiếp tục được điều tra, làm rõ để xử lý theo quy định của pháp luật.
Qua vụ việc, Công an xã An Biên khuyến cáo người dân cần bình tĩnh, kiềm chế, giải quyết các mâu thuẫn, tranh chấp bằng biện pháp phù hợp, đúng quy định của pháp luật; tuyệt đối không sử dụng bạo lực để giải quyết mâu thuẫn.
Đồng thời, đề nghị người dân không đăng tải, chia sẻ hoặc bình luận, lan truyền những thông tin sai sự thật, chưa được kiểm chứng liên quan đến vụ việc xảy ra tại Trường Trung học phổ thông An Biên. Các hành vi lợi dụng không gian mạng để đưa tin sai sự thật, xuyên tạc vụ việc, gây ảnh hưởng đến an ninh, trật tự sẽ bị xem xét, xử lý theo quy định của pháp luật. Người dân cần theo dõi, cập nhật thông tin từ các cơ quan chức năng và nguồn tin chính thống.
Theo Cổng TTĐT CA An Giang

articles.title: Homeowners tap equity as HELOC balances post biggest jump since 2005: New York Fed report
articles.text:
Homeowners tapped their home equity lines of credit in the third quarter at the highest rate in more than two decades, according to a new Federal Reserve Bank of New York report on household debt released Tuesday.
Balances on HELOCs jumped by $23 billion during the three months ending Sept. 30, the largest increase since 2005. That brings the outstanding amount owed to $481 billion, the report shows. This also marks the 18th consecutive quarterly increase.
HELOC balances peaked at roughly $714 billion in the first quarter of 2009, according to a 2015 New York Fed report.
The current rise in balances comes amid a sluggish housing market, due at least partly to the so-called mortgage rate lock-in effect. Just under half of outstanding mortgages — 49.1% — carried rates of 4% or lower in the second quarter, according to a Realtor.com analysis of federal mortgage data, leaving many owners reluctant to give up their low rates to purchase another home at current higher borrowing costs.
The median price of an existing home was $417,500 in September, according to the National Association of Realtors, a real estate trade group. While up just 1.3% from a year earlier, the amount is nearly 54% higher than in September 2019, according to NAR. The average rate on a typical 30-year fixed-rate mortgage is 7.3% as of Tuesday, according to Mortgage News Daily.
"HELOCs let them borrow against their equity without giving up the low interest rate on their home," said certified financial planner Douglas Boneparth, president and founder of Bone Fide Wealth in New York City and a member of CNBC's Financial Advisor Council.
Mortgage holders have $17.5 trillion in equity
Mortgage holders collectively had $17.5 trillion in home equity as of the third quarter, according to a new report from Intercontinental Exchange, or ICE, a financial markets technology and data company.
Tappable equity that can be accessed — meaning a homeowner's equity would remain at or above 20% of the home's value after tapping it — rose 1.2%, or $16,600, from a year ago to an average of $204,000 per borrower, the ICE report shows.
"Homeowners are sitting on substantial housing wealth, with 2.4 million mortgage holders now holding at least $1 million in equity," Andy Walden, head of mortgage and Housing Market Research at ICE, said in the report.
Average HELOC rate is 7.49%
HELOCs let you tap a line of credit over time as you need the money, instead of getting it all at once like a home equity loan or cash-out refinance.
While HELOCs may have fewer up-front costs than a home equity loan, they generally have a variable interest rate. This means it will move up and down based on a benchmark like the prime rate, which banks use as a basis to set rates on a variety of loans. And, while the Federal Reserve doesn't control that rate, it is influenced by changes the Fed makes to the so-called federal funds rate.
"If your budget only works at today's rate, then your budget doesn't really work," Boneparth said of HELOCs. "You kind of have to be mindful of the fact that rates may go up."
If your budget only works at today's rate, then your budget doesn't really work.Douglas BoneparthPresident and founder of Bone Fide Wealth
The average interest rate for a $30,000 HELOC was 7.49% as of Nov. 4, according to Bankrate.
Many HELOCs also have a "draw" period when you can take money out, which often lasts five or 10 years. During that time, you typically are only required to pay the interest on any funds you've withdrawn. After that, however, you'll enter a repayment period of, say, 10 or 20 years, when you're required to pay both interest and principal. Because of that, your payments will jump if you've only been paying interest.
"The real test comes when the repayment period kicks in, and the principal starts to show up, if that's how their HELOC is structured," Boneparth said. "Payments potentially could double overnight, and you really want to know that before you sign anything."
Additionally, consider what you're planning to use the money for, Boneparth said.
"If you're borrowing against your home to improve your home, that could make a lot of sense," Boneparth said. "Borrowing against your house to pay off credit cards is a little trickier because you're turning unsecured debt into debt secured by the roof over your head."
In that case, if your spending habits don't change, he said, "you're just moving the problem somewhere a little scarier."

articles.title: Tất cả người dân cả nước chú ý quy định xử phạt cư trú mới nhất đã áp dụng
articles.text:
Tất cả người dân cả nước chú ý quy định xử phạt cư trú mới nhất đã áp dụng
Trong trường hợp khách đến nhà ngủ qua đêm không khai báo lưu trú, chủ nhà bị phạt thế nào?
- 31-07-2026Người dân ở những khu vực sau cần chú ý: Có thể được kiểm tra cư trú đột xuất theo quy định
- 31-07-2026Thông tin quan trọng về cư trú đã có hiệu lực, tất cả người dân chú ý
Từ ngày 01/7/2026, các quy định mới về thông báo lưu trú chính thức có hiệu lực theo Luật sửa đổi, bổ sung một số điều của 10 Luật có liên quan đến an ninh, trật tự số 118/2025/QH15. Sự thay đổi này đặt ra trách nhiệm pháp lý rõ ràng hơn cho các hộ gia đình khi có khách đến ngủ qua đêm, đồng thời đưa ra chế tài xử phạt cụ thể đối với những trường hợp chây ì hoặc quên không khai báo.
Trách nhiệm thông báo lưu trú khi có khách ngủ qua đêm
Căn cứ theo quy định mới bổ sung vào Điều 30 Luật Cư trú 2020, từ ngày 01/7/2026, khi có người đến lưu trú qua đêm tại chỗ ở của cá nhân hoặc hộ gia đình, thành viên trong gia đình có trách nhiệm thực hiện việc thông báo lưu trú với cơ quan đăng ký cư trú. Trong trường hợp khách đến lưu trú nhưng các thành viên hộ gia đình lại không có mặt tại chỗ ở đó, chính người khách lưu trú sẽ phải tự chịu trách nhiệm thực hiện thủ tục khai báo này.
Về thời hạn thực hiện, pháp luật quy định việc thông báo lưu trú phải được hoàn thành trước 23 giờ của ngày bắt đầu lưu trú. Đối với những trường hợp khách đến sau 23 giờ, thời hạn khai báo được nới lỏng nhưng phải được hoàn thành trước 08 giờ sáng ngày hôm sau.
Mức xử phạt hành chính khi không khai báo lưu trú
Nhiều người thường băn khoăn liệu việc quên khai báo khi có bạn bè, người thân đến ngủ qua đêm có bị xử lý hay không. Theo quy định, hành vi không thực hiện đúng quy định về thông báo lưu trú sẽ bị xử lý nghiêm khắc tùy theo tính chất của chủ thể vi phạm:
Đối với cá nhân, hộ gia đình: Hành vi không thực hiện đúng quy định về thông báo lưu trú có thể bị áp dụng hình thức xử lý từ phạt cảnh cáo hoặc phạt tiền từ 500.000 đồng đến 1.000.000 đồng.
Đối với các cơ sở kinh doanh lưu trú, nhà ở tập thể, cơ sở du lịch: Mức phạt tiền sẽ được tính toán bậc thang dựa trên số lượng người lưu trú không được khai báo:
Phạt tiền từ 2 đến 4 triệu đồng nếu vi phạm đối với từ 01 đến 03 người.
Phạt tiền từ 4 đến 8 triệu đồng đối với trường hợp vi phạm từ 04 đến 08 người.
Phạt tiền từ 8 đến 12 triệu đồng nếu số lượng không khai báo từ 09 người trở lên.
Lưu ý: Các mức phạt trên áp dụng cho cá nhân; nếu chủ thể vi phạm là tổ chức, mức phạt tiền sẽ tăng gấp đôi (bằng 02 lần mức phạt đối với cá nhân).
Trong đó, nội dung thông báo về lưu trú phải bao gồm: Họ và tên, ngày, tháng, năm sinh, số định danh cá nhân hoặc số hộ chiếu của người lưu trú; lý do lưu trú; thời gian lưu trú; địa chỉ lưu trú.
Thời hạn thực hiện việc lưu trú được quy định như sau: Việc thông báo lưu trú được thực hiện trước 23 giờ của ngày bắt đầu lưu trú; trường hợp người đến lưu trú sau 23 giờ thì việc thông báo lưu trú được thực hiện trước 08 giờ ngày hôm sau.
Hướng dẫn cách thông báo lưu trú nhanh chóng qua ứng dụng VNeID
Nhằm tạo sự thuận lợi tối đa cho người dân trong việc chấp hành quy định pháp luật mà không mất nhiều thời gian đi lại, cơ quan chức năng đã tích hợp tính năng khai báo trực tuyến. Người dân hoàn toàn có thể chủ động thực hiện thông báo lưu trú ngay trên điện thoại thông minh thông qua ứng dụng định danh quốc gia VNeID theo các bước sau:
Bước 1: Đăng nhập vào ứng dụng VNeID trên thiết bị di động.
Bước 2: Tại màn hình chính, ấn chọn mục “Thủ tục hành chính”, sau đó chọn tiếp tính năng “Thông báo lưu trú”.
Bước 3: Giao diện mới hiển thị, người thực hiện tiến hành kê khai đầy đủ các thông tin bắt buộc bao gồm: Địa chỉ cơ quan, cơ quan công an tiếp nhận và thông tin chi tiết về cơ sở lưu trú.
Bước 4: Bấm xác nhận các thông tin vừa điền, tiếp tục chọn “Thêm người lưu trú”. Nếu người thông báo đồng thời là người lưu trú, hãy tích chọn ô tương ứng và điền đầy đủ các thông tin cá nhân, lý do lưu trú cũng như khoảng thời gian lưu trú cụ thể.
Bước 5: Kiểm tra lại toàn bộ dữ liệu, sau đó bấm “Lưu” và “Gửi yêu cầu” để hoàn tất quá trình khai báo với cơ quan công an.
Việc nắm bắt và tuân thủ đúng thời hạn khai báo lưu trú không chỉ giúp người dân tránh được các mức phạt hành chính không đáng có mà còn góp phần chung tay đảm bảo an ninh trật tự tại địa phương.

articles.title: Small caps have lagged large stocks in the past decade. Why Baron Capital sees a turnaround
articles.text: Small caps are pulling ahead, and Baron Capital thinks they have further to go. The small-cap index Russell 2000 is up 13% in 2026, ahead of the S & P 500's nearly 10% advance in that time. That lead held through a bruising week for stocks after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress — and investors grew concerned that the election results could slow the artificial intelligence data center build-out. "The outlook is strong" for small caps, Cliff Greenberg, portfolio manager of Baron Capital's small-cap fund, said Friday at the asset manager's investment conference in New York City. .RUT .SPX YTD mountain Russell 2000 index vs. S & P 500 performance YTD Greenberg said nearly a decade of underperformance versus larger companies has left small caps relatively cheap and overlooked by investors. The Russell 2000 has returned 159% to investors over the past 10 years, while the S & P 500's total return in that time exceeds 300%. However, the Russell trades at 16 times trailing 12-month earnings, a sharp discount to the S & P 500's multiple of roughly 25, FactSet data shows. He added that cooling inflation could boost smaller stocks. Investors may have to be patient on that front after the latest consumer price index report came in hotter than expected. Yet, Brent and WTI oil prices are down 12% and 6%, respectively, over the past month. If oil keeps falling, it could ease inflationary pressures. Greenberg's fund, Baron Small Cap Fund (BSCFX) has gained 8% this quarter. It's up about 3% in 2026. Some of the fund's holdings include industrial stock Vertiv , tech company Guidewire , casino operator Red Rock Resorts and healthcare name RadNet . Overall, the fund's weighting is skewed toward industrials which account for 30% of the holdings , followed by information technology at 22.4%. Here are four names Greenberg highlighted at last week's conference. Shake Shack Greenberg sees room for Shake Shack to open more restaurants, contributing to its long growth runway. Shake Shack said last week it opened 21 new company-operated Shacks in the third quarter and is targeting 1,500 locations for the long term. Baron Capital initiated a position in Shake Shack in the second quarter. Greenberg also called out Shake Shack stock's cheap valuation. Its forward PE ratio of about 59 is far below a five-year average of 162. Shares of Shake Shack are up almost 15% over the past month. Waste Connections Greenberg pointed to Waste Connections for the solid waste services company's strong market share and attractive valuation. The Woodlands, Texas-based company is the third largest solid waste company in North America. The company collects and disposes of waste for about 9 million customers across 46 U.S. states and six Canadian provinces. Its current business mix includes about 40% under exclusive or franchise contracts and 60% in competitive markets. Its revenue mix is largely skewed to the U.S., which accounts for 86% of sales, while Canada accounts for the remaining 14%. Shares are up more than 8% in 2026. Doncasters The Baron Capital portfolio manager is also excited about Doncasters, which is under DPC Holdings . Doncasters is an independent manufacturer of highly engineered engine products, including precision cast components. The company's main end markets are aerospace and industrial gas turbines. Doncasters' exposure to the industrial gas turbine market as a percentage of revenue is greater in comparison to its larger competitors, Rothschild & Co noted in July. Doncasters went public in June. The stock initially popped after its IPO but is down 22% over the past month. Texas Roadhouse The firm is also an investor in Texas Roadhouse . The casual dining chain known for its steaks, ribs and bread at affordable prices has opened 830 restaurants across 49 states since it first opened in 1993 . It also owns other restaurants including Bubba's 33 and Jaggers. Greenberg likes how management continues to open restaurants and expand its footprint. According to the company's third-quarter report released last week, Texas Roadhouse opened five company-owned locations, which included two Bubba's and one Jaggers restaurant. The company has over 15 openings scheduled for the fourth quarter and remains on track to open about 35 restaurants across the three brands in 2026. Shares are up about 17% over the past year.

articles.title: Camera cặp đôi ghé hàng loạt tiệm rau củ, giở chiêu đưa 500.000 đồng để lừa tiền thừa
articles.text:
Camera cặp đôi ghé hàng loạt tiệm rau củ, giở chiêu đưa 500.000 đồng để lừa tiền thừa
Danh tính của hai đối tượng xuất hiện trong clip đã được nhanh chóng xác minh.
Thời gian qua, mạng xã hội lan truyền đoạn camera an ninh ghi lại cảnh cặp đôi đi xe máy dừng mua rau bên đường. Người phụ nữ mua rau rồi giả vờ đã đưa tớ 500 nghìn đồng cho người bán và nhất quyết đòi lại tiền thừa. Thực tế trong clip, người này chưa đưa tiền cho người bán. Sau khi lấy được tiền, cặp đôi nhanh chóng lên xe rời đi. Thủ đoạn của cặp đôi khiến dư luận bức xúc.
(Nguồn: Mạng xã hội)
Ngày 9/11, thông tin trên báo Bảo vệ Pháp luật, Công an TP Hồ Chí Minh cho biết, Công an xã Xuân Thới Sơn đã tạm giữ Nguyễn Trọng Nghĩa và Nguyễn Thị Ngọc Tuyết để điều tra hành vi “Lừa đảo chiếm đoạt tài sản”.
Qua công tác nắm bắt tình hình trên không gian mạng, Công an xã Xuân Thới Sơn phối hợp phòng Cảnh sát hình sự Công an TP Hồ Chí Minh phát hiện hai đối tượng có hành vi lừa đảo chiếm đoạt tài sản của các tiểu thương xảy ra trên địa bàn xã.
Công an xã Xuân Thới Sơn đã xác minh, mời Nguyễn Trọng Nghĩa (SN 1964, ngụ phường Tân Hòa, TP Hồ Chí Minh) và Nguyễn Thị Ngọc Tuyết (SN 1976, ngụ phường An Hội Tây, TP Hồ Chí Minh) để làm rõ hành vi trên.
Bên cạnh đó, Dân Việt thông tin thêm về kết quả điều tra, do không có nghề nghiệp ổn định, để có tiền tiêu xài, 2 đối tượng Tuyết và Nghĩa đã bàn bạc với nhau đi đến các tiệm bán hàng rau, củ quả… để mua những món hàng có giá từ 10 đến 20 nghìn đồng rồi dàn cảnh tình huống lộn xộn làm cho chủ hàng mất tập trung.
Sau đó, đối tượng Tuyết nói đã đưa số tiền 500 nghìn đồng và yêu cầu chủ hàng trả lại khoản tiền thừa. Tuy nhiên, trên thực tế, các đối tượng chưa đưa tiền cho chủ hàng. Với thủ đoạn như trên, hai đối tượng đã liên tục gây ra nhiều vụ việc chiếm đoạt tiền của nhiều chủ hàng trên địa bàn xã Xuân Thới Sơn và các địa bàn xung quanh.
Hiện Công an xã Xuân Thới Sơn phối hợp Phòng Cảnh sát hình sự Công an TP.HCM đang tiếp tục điều tra mở rộng vụ án.

articles.title: Nvidia hires law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead Jensen Huang affair probe
articles.text:
Nvidia's board of directors said on Tuesday that it hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang and whether company secrets or national security was compromised, after Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman who has been connected to Chinese intelligence.
"The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday," the board said in a statement.
Kim joined the firm last month, and he was previously the chief U.S. prosecutor in Manhattan, according to Law360.
Nvidia has been thrust into turmoil since Huang's acknowledgement of the affair over the weekend. The chipmaker's stock dropped 6% on Tuesday after falling more than 4% on Monday, as investors worry that the investigation and scandal could result in the co-founder and CEO being forced out.
Nvidia and the board are facing pressure from critics and politicians over what the company knew about sales of its restricted AI chips to Chinese companies.
Over the past few weeks, The New York Times and Financial Times have reported that U.S. intelligence agencies surveilled an Asian technology executive, Alice Huang, who has been affiliated with Nvidia customer Megaspeed. These agencies have concluded that she is passing information to Beijing and is involved with Chinese intelligence, according to the reports.
Huang has become the face of the AI industry, going by his first name "Jensen" to customers and rivals as Nvidia's technology is used to train nearly all major AI models. The chipmaker has become an essential source of financing for AI startups and Huang has met with presidents and CEOs around the world as Nvidia's public face.
But Huang's actions have thrown the chipmaker into instability as he admitted to an affair with Alice Huang in an email to staff on Sunday.
"My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote in the message, while emphasizing that he is an American and supports U.S. national security.
An Nvidia representative said at the time that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption.
On Sunday, Nvidia's board said that it would investigate the allegations that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
Nvidia's board also said on Sunday that it has no reason to believe either national security nor Nvidia secrets were compromised.

articles.title: Before taking an employee buyout, make these 3 considerations, says employment law attorney
articles.text:
Layoffs are not the only way companies are shrinking their workforces.
Two major companies in different industries announced employee buyouts on Oct. 26. Microsoft announced plans to extend buyout packages to a quarter of the company. Media and entertainment company Skydance said in a memo to employees that it will offer buyouts to an undisclosed number of workers, according to Reuters. The memo also introduced a five-day, return-to-office mandate for all employees. The announcements sparked fears of potential layoffs at the companies on Reddit and other social media platforms.
Employee buyouts are voluntary and, in most cases, allow workers to leave their job in exchange for a severance package. Buyouts are "becoming more and more popular" as a way for employers to reduce their headcounts and, ultimately, cut costs, says Tammy Marzigliano, a plaintiff-side labor lawyer at Outten & Golden.
While buyouts can provide employees with a financial buffer as they transition into a new role or prepare for retirement, they also can signal layoffs are ahead, Marzigliano tells CNBC Make It.
For workers who feel they are not meeting expectations at work or have already been placed on a performance improvement plan, a voluntary buyout gives employees an exit with severance. A buyout may also be a good deal for professionals who plan to retire soon and employees who already want to leave the company.
But for workers who want to keep their jobs, buyouts can be yet another source of anxiety. Before Disney announced thousands of layoffs on Nov. 3, the company offered some of its executives voluntary early retirement offers in August. "Some of these circumstances could lead to pressure on the employees, and leaving them to feel like they don't really have a choice" to take a buyout, Marzigliano says.
If workers anticipate layoffs, a buyout might seem lucrative, but Marzigliano says the decision to take a buyout "deserves careful consideration." She recommends that employees review several employee documents, "assess their own personal situation" and watch the job market closely.
Assess your finances
Employees should first assess their offer letter, employee handbook and plan documents, Marzigliano says. These contracts often include information about benefits and perks, including vesting schedules, or the dates an employee is entitled to cash out various financial awards. For example, while employee contributions to a 401(k) automatically belong to the employee, a company's contributions might be bound by a schedule that determines when an employee receives access to those funds. Workers also risk losing out on other non-cash compensation like company equity.
A severance package might match an employee's salary for a few months, but Marzigliano says to consider the other financial awards you might lose upon signing a buyout agreement.
She also says to compare the voluntary buyout offer against what you'd receive in a layoff, under the company's reduction in force policy, which means the company has eliminated your position and has no plans of rehiring for the role in the future. The policy should state the benefits the company provides to workers, if any, and when employees should expect to receive their severance packages. If the reduction in force policy is more financially lucrative, it might be best to hold out.
Consider your employee benefits
A buyout could also cost workers their health insurance, which leaves them with several options. The Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, or COBRA, allows families to temporarily extend the coverage they received through their workplace for 18 months in cases of termination, though workers usually pay the full insurance premium, including the amount their employer once contributed, and a 2% fee.
Workers can also enroll in a government-regulated ACA plan, but eligibility requirements for subsidies vary by state and some will see a double-digit rate increase on premiums in 2027. Workers should consult their plan provider and assess their severance package to see how much of their premium they will be required to pay out of pocket, according to the U.S. Department of Labor website.
An employee might also forfeit or delay their unemployment benefits upon signing a buyout agreement because it could be considered a voluntary exit . Unemployment benefits, and who qualifies, vary by state, so workers should consult their state's resources. A buyout agreement might also make an employee ineligible for rehire at the company based on the terms of their contract, Marzigliano says.
Beyond finances
Marzigliano says buyouts provide employees with a "cleaner exit" compared to layoffs because employees get a greater say in their career trajectory. The agreement also offers employees the opportunity to leave their job with certainty and a financial runway, which could provide some stability in a tough job market.
In some cases, though, buyouts also include confidentiality and non-disparagement agreements. These documents prevent employees from speaking out against the company in the future, according to Marzigliano. In the case an employee believes their employer discriminated against them for a protected characteristic, they may no longer be able to seek legal action against their employer.
The decision to take a buyout is a deeply personal one as it can also impact a worker's sense of identity and their family, according to Marzigliano.
"A buyout's not a gift; it's a transaction," Marzigliano says. "And [workers] should assess what they're giving up as much as what they're getting."

articles.title: Lý do HLV Kim Sang-sik không thể gạch tên Đình Bắc dù "cày ải" 46 trận đấu?
articles.text:
Lý do HLV Kim Sang-sik không thể gạch tên Đình Bắc dù "cày ải" 46 trận đấu?
HLV Kim Sang-sik tin tiền đạo Nguyễn Đình Bắc sở hữu thể trạng cùng ý chí chiến đấu tốt để tiếp tục cống hiến cho đội tuyển Việt Nam trong đợt tập trung tháng 11.
Trả lời báo chí trước trận giao hữu của đội tuyển Việt Nam với Đài Loan (Trung Quốc) diễn ra ngày 11/11, HLV Kim Sang-sik thừa nhận việc lựa chọn nhân sự đợt này gặp nhiều khó khăn do bão chấn thương và lịch thi đấu dày đặc. Dù vậy, nhà cầm quân người Hàn Quốc khẳng định không quá lo lắng về nguy cơ quá tải của tiền đạo Nguyễn Đình Bắc.
"Đình Bắc vẫn ổn dù phải thi đấu nhiều thời gian qua. Bản thân cậu ấy có ý chí chiến đấu mãnh liệt, khao khát thi đấu và tôi tin cậu ấy sẽ chơi tốt mỗi khi ra sân", HLV Kim Sang-sik cho biết.
Tính từ đầu năm 2026, chân sút sinh năm 2004 thuộc nhóm cầu thủ cày ải nhiều nhất Việt Nam với 46 trận đấu chính thức trên mọi cấp độ, trong màu áo ĐTQG, U23 và CLB Công an Hà Nội. Tần suất ra sân liên tục khiến tiền đạo quê Nghệ An xuất hiện dấu hiệu quá tải sau ASEAN Cup 2026.
Để ngăn ngừa rủi ro chấn thương, HLV Kim Sang-sik ở ĐTQG và HLV Mano Polking tại CAHN đã chủ động giảm thời gian thi đấu của Đình Bắc. Thực tế, chân sút này vẫn có lúc gặp sự cố đau nhẹ nhưng chỉ phải nghỉ ngắn ngày.
Ở cấp CLB, CAHN cũng là đội bóng Việt Nam có mật độ thi đấu dày nhất từ đầu mùa giải 2026-2027 khi thi đấu nhiều đấu trường, trọng tâm là V.League và AFC Champions League Elite. Điều này khiến nhiều tuyển thủ quốc gia không đạt thể trạng tốt nhất.
Sau trận thắng CA TP HCM tại vòng 7 V.League hôm 7/11, HLV Polking gửi lời cảm ơn đồng nghiệp Kim Sang-sik vì đã tiết chế khối lượng vận động cho học trò. Dù muốn Đình Bắc được nghỉ ngơi hoàn toàn, ông vẫn thấu hiểu tầm quan trọng của tiền đạo này trên tuyển: "Đình Bắc rất thích khoác áo đội tuyển. Chúng tôi hiểu điều đó và người hâm mộ cũng thích xem cậu ấy thi đấu. Hy vọng học trò của tôi sẽ không gặp chấn thương".
Đội tuyển Việt Nam đã hội quân từ ngày 8/11 tại Ninh Bình để chuẩn bị cho giải giao hữu trên sân Thiên Trường, lần lượt chạm trán Đài Loan (Trung Quốc) ngày 11/11 và Kyrgyzstan (17/11). Việc Asian Cup 2027 bị hoãn giúp nhóm trụ cột có thêm thời gian nghỉ ngơi, đồng thời buộc ban huấn luyện phải thay đổi kế hoạch nhân sự.
Từ mục tiêu rèn giũa chuẩn bị cho giải đấu châu Á tại Arab Saudi, HLV Kim Sang-sik chuyển hướng sang trao cơ hội cho nhiều tố chất mới. Trong 24 cầu thủ được triệu tập đợt này, có tới 19 người thi đấu dưới 5 trận cho ĐTQG, bao gồm 11 tân binh chưa từng ra mắt.
"Việc Asian Cup 2027 bị hoãn khiến tôi, các cầu thủ và người hâm mộ đều nuối tiếc. Nhưng toàn đội vẫn phải nỗ lực hết mình để giành chiến thắng và tạo niềm vui cho người hâm mộ", HLV Kim chia sẻ.
Đồng quan điểm với thuyền trưởng người Hàn Quốc, tân đội trưởng Nguyễn Thành Chung xem đây là thời điểm thử nghiệm đội hình lý tưởng. Trung vệ sinh năm 1997 nhấn mạnh: "Càng nhiều nhân sự mới càng cho thấy chiều sâu của đội tuyển. Việc được triệu tập không đơn giản và là vinh dự rất lớn. Tôi thấy trong ánh mắt và từng bước chân của mỗi đồng đội sự nhiệt huyết, tinh thần tích cực cùng quyết tâm chiến thắng".

            Australian Dollar - Summary
The Australian dollar traded below $0.69, hovering at its lowest level since late March as weak domestic economic surveys and a stronger US dollar weighed on the currency. Consumer sentiment fell to a four-year low in November, while business conditions remained stuck in negative territory, a level not seen in six years, reflecting growing caution over the domestic economic outlook. The disappointing readings reinforced expectations that the Reserve Bank of Australia has finished its tightening cycle following five interest rate increases this year, which brought the cash rate to an eighteen-year high of 4.85%. Markets now imply an 82% probability that rates have peaked, with a quarter-point rate cut fully priced in by the end of 2027. In contrast, hotter-than-expected US core inflation, which rose 0.3% in October, lifted expectations for a potential 50-basis-point rate hike by the Federal Reserve next month, supporting the US dollar and adding pressure on the Aussie.

Traders also await RBA board member Marnie Baker’s speech on Thursday for further clues on the policy outlook.
